📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 06.05.2026 in den Kategorien Eredivisie,SV Academy,Tactical Theory,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

N.E.C. Nijmegen kon dit seizoen vanwege hun relationistische patronen en hun oplossingsstrategieën tegen mandekkingen met verticale positiewisselingen van hun centrale verdedigers op zich attent maken. Op de voorlaatste zondag ontmoetten zich in Rotterdam voor de Nederlandse bekerfinale AZ Alkmaar en het verrassende team van Nederland, N.E.C. Nijmegen. AZ won na een doelpunt uit een standaardsituatie in de eerste helft en goed uitgespeelde counters in de tweede helft uiteindelijk duidelijk met 5:1. Als kenner van de Nederlandse voetbalwereld heeft HH zich met de wedstrijd beziggehouden en beide teams nader onder de loep genomen.

N.E.C. speelde vanuit een 1-3-2-4-1 in balbezit en drukvol met man-tegen-man pressing, waarbij Linssen de keeper van AZ boogvormig aanliep. Over het algemeen probeerde N.E.C. bij elke gelegenheid door te drukken en in hun 1-1-structuur te komen. AZ had zich daarop ingesteld en hun 1-4-2-3-1-achtige basisformatie veranderd in een soort 1-4-2-2-2, waarbij Parrot en Daal de voorste linie vormden. AZ’s idee voor lange ballen tegen Nijmegens klassieke 1-1-pressing (intentie van balverovering in het directe duel door maximaal korte afstanden, onafhankelijk van dekking van de centrale, binnenste lijn) waren dwars- en diepteloopbewegingen tegen Nijmegens driemansdefensie (afgestemd op AZ’s 1-4-2-3-1), om maximaal veel verdedigers van Nijmegen te binden en vrije ruimtes naast en voor de laatste linie maximaal groot te maken. Daarbij driften Mijnans en Smit steeds weer slim in mogelijke kaats- of doorverbindingsruimtes voor en naast Parrot. Omdat Nijmegen vrijloopbewegingen direct volgde en geen collectieve laatste linie en hoogte koos, werden de verticale afstanden sterk uitgerekt. Vooral Sandler als centrale verdediger en directe tegenstander van Parrot fungeerde soms als libero ver achter zijn medeverdedigers. Een groot manco bij N.E.C. was sowieso dat een collectief opschuiven van de laatste linie, de organisatie van een gezamenlijke nieuwe hoogte niet of slechts zeer terughoudend en twijfelend plaatsvond. AZ maakte daar gebruik van met slimme loopwegen achter de lijnen en/of snel uitspelen van combinaties in de (grote) ruimte voor de laatste lijn van N.E.C.

De uitrekking en tegelijkertijd de fysieke aanwezigheid door Mijnans en Smit evenals de strijdlustige dubbele zes van Koopmeiners en Clasie kwam het 1-4-2-2-2 van AZ meer tegemoet. Soms leek het alsof juist deze verticale uitrekking (1-4-2-2-2, loopwegen van Parrot diep/wegtrekkend, Nijmegen zonder eigen buitenspellijn) evenals horizontale uitrekking (dwarslopen van Parrot, asynchroon/ aansluitend uitwijken van Mijnans) bewust door AZ gewild en voorbereid werd, doordat men vanuit een zeer brede 1-4-2-opbouw direct en vroeg lange passafstanden naar doelman Owusu-Oduro koos om het onmiddellijke aanlopen van Nijmegen (Linssen, waarbij de afstanden te groot waren om de bal serieus te kunnen onderscheppen) uit te lokken en daardoor eigen lange ballen goed te kunnen voorbereiden.

Wanneer AZ zich toch voor een korte opbouw besliste, vielen ze terug in een soort 1-3-1-opbouw met een naar binnen kwamende linkerback (de Wit). Opvallend was echter de duidelijke focus op de voorbereiding van lange ballen. Zo zocht bijvoorbeeld Koopmeiners in 1-3-2-opbouwmomenten, in plaats van de vrije ruimte te bezetten om druk te ontlasten, de directe weg naar voren om aanwezigheid voor tweede ballen te tonen.

AZ’s hybride 1-4-2-3-1 naar 1-5-2-2-1 als kryptoniet tegen N.E.C.

Recent findings suggest that bij balbezit van Nijmegen koos AZ voor een fundamentele spiegeling van N.E.C. Daarbij kozen zij voor een conservatief, mandekkend middenveldpressing. Terwijl Clasie (een zes van N.E.C.) en de beide tienen Daal en Mijnans (respectievelijk de halfverdedigers Dasa en Fonville) zeer klassiek vanuit het middenveldpressing balnabij mandekten en man-georiënteerd aanliepen, koos Parrot steeds weer slim voor diepere, passieve posities om alle wegen naar het centrum te sluiten.

According to recent reports, een bijzondere rol kwam toe aan Koopmeiners. Hij ging, uitgaande van een manoriëntatie tegen Nijmegens creatieve speler Chery, steeds weer bij de overgang naar een lager blok in de laatste linie en vormde zo een vijfmanslijn. In totaal ontstond zo een 1-5-2-2-1 in lagere fases van AZ door het terugvallen van Smit naar de dubbele zes met Clasie. Chery werd zo niet per se extreem mandekkend bewaakt, maar zijn actieradius naar voren werd beperkt en tegelijkertijd werd het noodzakelijke uitstappen van Koopmeiners uit de vijfmanslijn goed opgevangen.

In a recent development, de 1-5-2-2-1-structuur van AZ paste ook bij de meer relationistische intentie van N.E.C., waarbij het minder ging om balgeoriënteerde vrijloopbewegingen ten opzichte van elkaar, maar meer om vrij-radicaal een overtal in balnabijheid te creëren, minder afgestemd op elkaar of in relatie tot specifieke tegenstanderbewegingen/-posities. Zo kon de niet-balkant tien van AZ het centrum mede sluiten, loopwegen uit de opbouwlijn van N.E.C. onderscheppen en N.E.C.’s zessen dwingen om breder buiten het blok te spelen of hoger te positioneren, waardoor ze minder bij overtal situaties betrokken waren of de restverdediging verwaarloosden.

Sources indicate that tegelijkertijd was hij in de counter snel aanspeelbaar (korte maar verleggende passafstanden tegen counter-press na balwinst). De beide tienen van AZ waren verantwoordelijk voor het oppakken van de steeds weer verticaal opschuivende centrale verdedigers van N.E.C. In totaal slaagde AZ erin met deze structuur een +1 in de laatste linie te creëren, doordat Clasie zich dieper en eerder aan de niet-balkant tien (Lebreton) oriënteerde, Goes in de laatste lijn +1 tegen Linssen kon doorschuiven, de ruimte voor de verdediging met Smit werd verdicht en de beide centrale tienen het centrum sloten. Daarbij werd er minder geprobeerd om directe balveroveringen te realiseren, maar des te meer om acties naar voren te blokkeren en de balbezitter passief te controleren. Het leek alsof AZ langer probeerde de controle over posities en ruimtebezetting ten opzichte van elkaar te behouden dan N.E.C. dat met hun vele positiewisselingen en herstructureringen kon.

Wanneer AZ toch het pressingmoment activeerde, paste dat goed bij de opbouwstructuur van N.E.C. Meestal koos Parrot dan een centrum-sluitende, iets laargere positie ten opzichte van Sandler of een centrale verdediger van N.E.C. Wanneer N.E.C. vervolgens via de halfverdedigers indribbeld, werden de afstanden in hun eerste opbouwlinie automatisch groter. Het indribbelen van de halfverdedigers kon door de tienen van AZ goed worden opgevangen, een terugpass werd in de beweging door de eerder uitgestapte tien doorgelopen en Parrot nam verticale vervolgbewegingen van de passerende halfverdediger over. Door de grotere passafstand (door het vroege indribbelen) werd de loopactie van de passer minder effectief, omdat de bal langer onderweg was en de druk van AZ op (meestal) Sandler goed kon worden behouden. Korte passafstanden bij N.E.C. voor een lokkend spel en bewegen werden zo opgelost, mede omdat Nejasmic in pressingoplossingen als derde man geen sterke prestatie leverde. AZ liep echter vaak niet door tot Cillessen, die desondanks vaak zonder druk voor de lange bal koos (die zoals eerder beschreven geen effectief middel was).

Zonder indribbelen liep het voor N.E.C. ook niet beter, want doordat Sandler graag vanuit diepere posities lange passes probeert te spelen (Schlotterbeck-Vibes), moet N.E.C. bij het opschuiven grotere afstanden overbruggen met de laatste linie. Dit lukte slechts onregelmatig, waardoor de aansluiting van de laatste linie onvoldoende was.

Recent findings suggest that desalniettemin liet N.E.C. in de eerste helft, vaker via rechts, goede aanzetten zien om vanuit de zijkanten kansen te creëren. Een aanvallend probleem dat zich gedurende de hele wedstrijd voordeed, was dat acties vanaf de zijkant naar binnen niet ruimer (dus dynamisch ruimtes richting het centrum openen) of doelgerichter (loopacties in de rug van de balkant centrale verdediger) werden bevoordeeld. De aansluitende bewegingen om tegenstanders bewust weg te trekken van de vrijgespeelde zijkant kwamen te weinig voor. In plaats daarvan werden mogelijke passroutes naar binnen soms dichtgelopen door passief achter de bal aan te lopen (om een korte passoptie te zijn?). Een “Escadinha”, dus een diagonale positionering van meerdere spelers als een “ladder” naar voren, idealiter richting het doel, zou ook een goed middel zijn geweest om de relationistische patronen van N.E.C. om te zetten in gevaarlijkere situaties voor het doel, maar werd niet gecreëerd. Vooral via Sano als vrije, hoger doorschuivende, licht niet-balkant zes had men via een precieze halfspace-halfspace-verplaatsing (tegen mandekkingsteams sowieso altijd effectief) tot afwerkposities kunnen komen. Vooral links met Koopmeiners en rechts met Goes, die beiden bezig waren met het dekken op de lijn van de balkant nummer tien van N.E.C., had men goed ruimtes in hun rug kunnen bezetten en bespelen – zowel achter als voor de laatste linie van AZ. Een paar keer, wanneer het N.E.C. lukte om van buiten naar binnen achter de balkant centrale verdediger te opereren, werd het ook meteen gevaarlijk. Op die momenten werden door de duo’s van N.E.C. (N.E.C. gebruikt de duo’s op de zijkant enigszins vergelijkbaar met Bayern in voor- of achterlopende, doorlopende bewegingen) (Ouaissa-Chery/Dasa en Önal-Lebreton/Fonville) natuurlijke verdedigingsmechanismen uitgelokt (achter de back spelen = centrale verdediger die uitstapte zal waarschijnlijk in de laatste lijn terugvallen, afdekken of doordekken), waardoor N.E.C., gecombineerd met goed wegbewegen van de tegenstander, zich in de rug van de verdediging enkele (halve) kansen kon creëren. AZ loste deze kleine problemen in de controle op doordat Clasie zich als niet-balkant zes toch meer balgeoriënteerd positioneerde, en Lebreton minder klassiek volgde.

Lange ballen van N.E.C. tegen een al terugzakkend AZ, dat snel naar achteren liep om diepte te sluiten, waren niet kansrijk – noch dynamisch noch numeriek.

In de tweede helft probeerde N.E.C. meer via een opdribbel van Fonville over de linkerkant te overloaden. Nejasmic koos een duidelijk meer centrumhoudende positionering in balbezit (zessen gestaffeld), Lebreton speelde als linker wing-back, de ingevallen Willumsson iets dieper, vermoedelijk om Goes van AZ uit de verdediging te trekken. Sano, de oprukkende Fonville en gedeeltelijk ook Chery namen deel aan de overload links. Een intentie leek te zijn om links aan te lokken om vervolgens rechts uit te spelen en Ouaissa in 1-tegen-1-duels te krijgen. Koopmeiners volgde Chery echter niet consequent, N.E.C. stond gedeeltelijk met 6-7 spelers in de linker halfspace, omdat zelfs Dasa (!) naar die kant ging. De bewegingen in deze overload waren echter zelden goed genoeg op elkaar afgestemd. De nog steeds aanwezige ruimtes (ook omdat AZ al vroeg balnabij met hun 4/5-mansketen kantelde en beide backs de Wit en Dijkstra individuele zwaktes hebben in het verdedigen van de rug) van buiten naar binnen in de rug (achter of voor de verdedigingslinie van AZ) van de half-uitstappende Goes werden te zelden consequent bespeeld of pas te laat bezet. Voorwaartse, boogvormige bewegingssequenties rondom een doelspeler, die positiegetrouw een ruimte bezet en als kaatsspeler fungeert, werden niet ingezet, waardoor alle bewegingen ten opzichte van elkaar geïmproviseerd of fragmentarisch leken. Wanneer men er eenmaal in slaagde een pocket in de halfspace tussen meerdere AZ-spelers te openen, werd deze geopende ruimte niet verder benut door bijvoorbeeld een tegenstanderbindende loopactie achter deze ruimte, maar probeerde elke speler eerder een beetje dominant de bal op te halen en verder te passen. Kort gezegd waren er veel dominante spelers die allemaal graag de bal direct en zonder intentie van elkaar wilden hebben. Aanvullende, ondersteunende intenties bij spelers waren zeldzaam. Waar men in de eerste helft nog vroeg een flankbezetting koos en zo een duo op de flank ruimte gaf, was Linssen nu de enige speler van N.E.C. in de box tegen AZ, dat consequent een +1 behield. Wanneer N.E.C. via de goed, maar nog te terughoudend, niet tot het einde van het mogelijke oprukpotentieel indribbelende Fonville wist op te rukken, ontbrak het aan activiteit en aansluitende bewegingen om via een snelle korte verplaatsing van afzakkende/verbindende zessen/centrale verdedigers de ontstane ruimtes in het centrum te bespelen. Vooral Willumsson bood hier geen goede passopties, hoewel hij zich in kansrijke ruimtes bevond. Ondanks het gebrek aan doorbraak kon N.E.C. meer controle over de wedstrijd verkrijgen en AZ enigszins naar achteren drukken. AZ daarentegen ging vanaf ongeveer de 55e minuut als reactie agressiever pressen, Goes volgde in hogere middenveldpressingfasen Willumsson ver naar voren. N.E.C. slaagde er niet in om tijdig in mandekking-oplossende patronen te komen, ook het spel via de extra speler Cillessen bracht geen verlichting. De communicatie van Sano en Nejasmic met betrekking tot afgestemd vrijlopen en vrijmaken, bewegingen naar de bal, liet te wensen over.

De invalbeurt van Willumsson bracht echter defensieve meerwaarde. De 193 cm grote IJslander kon bij lange ballen van AZ meer ruimte afdekken en met grotere actieradius meer aanwezigheid tonen bij tweede ballen, zonder gaten in de mandekking als tien op AZ’s zessen te trekken. N.E.C. paste namelijk Nejasmic aan in de rol van ondersteunende speler van Sandler. De zes koos nu zijn positioneringen zodanig dat hij direct rond/met Sandler tegen Parrot verdedigde en hem afschermde, waardoor vaak een soort viermanslijn bij N.E.C. ontstond, wat AZ voorlopig in toom hield.

In a recent development, N.E.C. probeerde nog steeds van links naar rechts uit te spelen. Helaas moesten ze de problemen in de restverdediging evenals de lasten van hun over-overload duur bekopen, omdat AZ twee keer na een verplaatsing naar Ouaissa balveroveringen boekte, counters startte en N.E.C.’s individuele rest-mandekking uiteindelijk meedogenloos afstrafte met de doelpunten voor 2:0 en 3:0. Vooral bij het tweede doelpunt werd duidelijk dat de individuele oriëntatie op de tegenstander, bijna onafhankelijk van de balpositie op het veld en zonder collectieve afstemming, duidelijke nadelen met zich meebrengt. Sowieso is mandekking rond het eigen zestien een minder logisch middel – zonder baldruk en collectieve hoogtebepaling van een laatste verdedigingslinie wordt het een uitnodiging om kansen te creëren. Bij de 2:0 door Mijnans lag het centrum voor het doel van Nijmegen open, bij de 3:0 werd er niet onderling gekanteld. Aan beide doelpunten ging echter een overloadpoging links vooraf, beter gezegd een over-overloadpoging. Klassieke overloadings met één, misschien twee extra spelers hebben als effect de tegenstander (idealiter) kort in een buitenruimte te binden zonder dat hij toegang tot balverovering heeft, vervolgens in voorbereide structuren (passafstanden zo groot als mogelijk voor zo min mogelijk balstops, maar zo kort als nodig om het overloadingseffect te benutten) te verplaatsen en de vrijere kant via 1-tegen-1, kleine-aantallenpatronen of voorzetten uit de halfspace te benutten. Bij een over-overload in de zin van het relationisme gaat het minder om goed gebalanceerde verplaatsingsstructuren, kleine-aantallenpatronen op de vrijere kant of een gezonde numerieke verhouding, maar om het doorspelen aan de overload kant. N.E.C. over-overload links, verplaatste dan relatief ruim (dus niet kort) via de centrale verdedigers via Dasa naar Ouaissa, waarbij AZ kortstondig een numeriek overwicht had aan de “vrijere” rechterkant. Bij balbezit van Ouaissa vóór de 2:0 stonden 5 (!) spelers van N.E.C. nog links functieloos, niet betrokken naast elkaar – dus ook aansluitende bewegingen om kleine-aantallenpatronen te ondersteunen of doelgerichte loopacties en voorzetvoorbereidingen ontbraken. Sandler, die de verplaatsing bij de 2:0 inleidde, liep na zijn pass naar de zijkant door naar voren (kennelijk een principe van Nijmegen). Echter op zo’n manier dat hij Ouaissa in het 1-tegen-1 blokkeerde, daarna niet als ondersteunende speler fungeerde en eigenlijk enigszins doelloos voor hem stond. Door de loopactie van Sandler liet Nejasmic zich duidelijk in de laatste linie zakken en ook Dasa zag ervan af om Ouaissa korter te ondersteunen, waardoor hij in een 1-tegen-2 terechtkwam. Uiteindelijk leidde dit door de ondertal-situatie tot balverlies van Nijmegen – mede door het ontbreken van een “bodyguard” van Dasa. Sandler stond voor de bal, het centrum was onbezet, AZ kon eenvoudig naar voren spelen en aanvallen – doordat het in de restverdediging ontbrak aan situatie-inzicht (Nejasmic) en consequente afdekking. Uiteindelijk verslechterde Sandlers loopactie de situatie eerder.

Ook aan de derde tegentreffer ging een verplaatsing van links naar rechts vooraf, dit keer liep Dasa als passer niet door – wat in tegenstelling tot Sandler bij de tweede tegentreffer passend zou zijn geweest – maar bood zich opnieuw kort aan – echter verloor Ouaissa zich opnieuw in een ondertal-dribbel (individuele besluitvorming, maar ook weinig ondersteuning). Dit keer was de situatie echter ideaal voor counter-press, waartoe de omliggende Nijmegen-spelers ook besloten, alleen dekte Dasa niet door, waardoor AZ min of meer gecontroleerd kon uitspelen. Met enig geluk wist AZ, opnieuw achter de laatste verdediger (Sandler) van N.E.C., maar nog op eigen helft, door te spelen en de 3:0 te maken. In het vervolg probeerde Nijmegen alles, maar behalve korte hoop na de 3:1 kwam er niets meer.

N.E.C. draaide zo ver aan de knop van positiewisselingen dat het bijna oververhit raakte. Constante over-overloads, nieuwe posities, verticaal doordribbelende centrale verdedigers uit een driemansopbouw zijn een grote, in deze wedstrijd tegen een slim verdedigend AZ, te grote last om tegelijkertijd spelritme, veldcontrole en restorganisatie in het oog te houden. Te veel spelers, bijvoorbeeld Sano als linker, afzakkende zes uit de overload, die bij balbezit van Ouaissa twee keer niet consequent genoeg naast de laatste verdediger van N.E.C. doorschoof voor een 2-tegen-1-afdekking, moeten in situaties verdedigen of aanvallen (Sandler voor de 2:0) die te vreemd/te ongeschikt of te veeleisend zijn qua situatiedynamiek voor hun profiel.

It has been revealed that desondanks is Nijmegen een team dat zich door hun vrij-radicale speelstijl heeft toegelegd op aantrekkelijk, onderhoudend voetbal. Uitstekende aanzetten zouden offensief door eenvoud, consistentie (positiegetrouwheid) en teamorganisatie (ritme van de aanvalsrichting, balans van overloads) kunnen worden verbeterd. Defensief zou een collectiviteit van de laatste linie zijn intrede moeten doen. Mocht dit in de toekomst lukken, zal N.E.C. niet alleen als een van de spannendste teams van Nederland voor ophef zorgen, maar ook in Europa. Als derde in de Eredivisie zijn ze in ieder geval op de goede weg.

HH groeide op aan de Nederlandse grens, maar oriënteerde zich tactisch liever richting Zuid-Europa. Naast freelancewerkzaamheden voor Duitse profclubs is hij sinds twee jaar ook actief als jeugdtrainer bij de O17 van N.E.C. Nijmegen.

Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!

It is officially Thanksgiving week, and if you're an NFL fan, that means you should probably just go ahead and clear your schedule from now until the end of the month because there is going to be an NFL game on almost every day.

In a recent development, that means there will be at least one game in six of the next eight days. Is that more football than I need? Probably, but I always eat more turkey than I need on Thanksgiving and never regret it, so I don't think I'll regret it if I watch every game between now and Nov. 30.

You also won't regret reading today's newsletter, so let's get to the rundown.

Sources indicate that welcome to my favorite part of the Monday newsletter: The part where I hand out grades for every team that played. The easiest grade to hand out this week went to the 49ers, who destroyed the Vikings in an NFC Showdown. The 49ers spent the entire week practicing in Colorado to get prepared for the 7,350-foot elevation in Mexico City, and it definitely showed.

With that in mind, let's get to a few of the grades from Week 11:.

As for the other grades that we've handed out so far in Week 11, you can check those out here.

You can't have a week of NFL action without winners and losers, so here are some of them. Carter Bahns put together this week's list of winners and losers, and we'll check out his losers below. It was such an ugly week for the Steelers that he actually put them down twice on this list.

If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here.

Everyone on the internet loves to overreact, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Zach Pereles looked at several things that happened during Week 11, so decide for yourself whether we're all overreacting.

In a recent development, statement: Jesse Minter will be one-and-done in Baltimore.Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. Lots of the Ravens' complications are out of first-year coach Jesse Minter's control. The Lamar Jackson injuries, obviously, threw the season way off course. Even Sunday's game was another example of the things Minter can't control going wrong. Justice Hill fumbled 1 yard from the end zone. LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, one of which the Panthers recovered. Derrick Henry also lost a fumble. It's been a season from hell. But there are plenty of issues Minter has been responsible for — or at least hasn't fixed — this year. Regarded as a defensive whiz after two years as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, he now oversees a defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in yards per game and yards per play, and in the bottom 10 in yards per pass attempt and takeaways. Simply put, it's been underwhelming at best for a team expected to contend for a championship. But the Ravens won't fire Minter at season's end. There are big-picture questions about Jackson and the entire roster, but Minter should get an offseason to tweak and improve his defense and fit it better to his defenders.

Statement: The Buccaneers have a serious Baker Mayfield problem.Overreaction or reality: Reality. The Buccaneers extended Mayfield with a three-year, $165 million deal just before the season began, after it seemed like an extension wouldn't happen. Tampa Bay must be wishing it hadn't made the deal. Mayfield is constantly banged up - he's dealing with plantar fasciitis in addition to the thumb injury that caused him to miss several games already this year - and he can't physically make his play style work. How the Buccaneers overcome this is TBD, because there are no realistic easy answers.

Statement: Jahmyr Gibbs will win Offensive Player of the Year. Overreaction or reality: Reality. It wasn't always pretty, but Jahmyr Gibbs ground out 118 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. He's up to 1,502 yards from scrimmage this season and on pace to finish with 2,553. That would break Chris Johnson's all-time record of 2,509 from 2009. That, one would think, would clinch an Offensive Player of the Year award for Gibbs. Even if he doesn't break the record, Gibbs would be a deserving winner, so long as he keeps producing. He's had at least 110 yards from scrimmage in all but two games.

There are plenty more overreactions, and you can check them out here.

Bech vede nel difensore un possibile punto fermo della Danimarca e considera aperto il futuro contrattuale dell’esterno.

It has been revealed that gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard stanno vivendo un momento di forma che, secondo il giornalista danese Malthe Bech di Bold, ha dato a entrambi un ruolo importante nella nazionale. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, I due giocatori della Lazio sono anche al centro dell’attenzione sul mercato italiano e internazionale. Bech ha parlato del loro rendimento, della squadra di Gennaro Gattuso e del percorso che li ha portati fin qui.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Bech non si aspettava di trovare la Lazio al primo posto in Serie A a questo punto del campionato. Immaginava che i biancocelesti potessero competere per un piazzamento tra le prime cinque, ma non un avvio così positivo: «Sono molto sorpreso da quanto bene abbia iniziato la stagione la Lazio. Mi aspettavo che lottasse per un posto tra le prime cinque, ma certamente non avrei immaginato di vederla in testa alla classifica della Serie A a questo punto del campionato».

Il giornalista considera Isaksen e Provstgaard tra i danesi più in forma della stagione. Entrambi, racconta, hanno ricevuto apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico Brian Riemer e occupano posizioni di rilievo nella nazionale: «Gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard sono due dei calciatori danesi che stanno attraversando il miglior momento di forma in questa stagione. Entrambi hanno ricevuto numerosi apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico della Danimarca, Brian Riemer, e ricoprono anche ruoli molto importanti nella nazionale.».

According to recent reports, in nazionale Isaksen è un riferimento per l’attacco, soprattutto sulla destra. Bech descrive così il suo coinvolgimento nel gioco danese: «Isaksen è uno dei principali riferimenti offensivi della Danimarca: gran parte della manovra d'attacco della squadra passa dai suoi piedi, soprattutto sulla fascia destra.».

Recent findings suggest that L’esterno ha iniziato la stagione in modo convincente. Per Bech, se manterrà questo rendimento, potrà disputare la migliore annata della sua carriera. Il giornalista indica finora come suo riferimento la stagione 2022/23, chiusa da capocannoniere della Superliga danese. In quell’annata Isaksen segnò anche due gol contro la Lazio: Bech ritiene probabile che il club biancoceleste abbia cominciato allora a interessarsi a lui.

Sul contratto, Bech ritiene che il giocatore sarebbe disponibile a prolungare l’accordo con la Lazio, ma lascia aperte le possibilità: alla scadenza mancano meno di due anni. A suo giudizio Isaksen sembra felice a Roma e a proprio agio in Italia, come il calciatore stesso ha dichiarato in più occasioni.

#153416. Latest Update: Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

Latest Update: Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1435 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected.
  • It has been revealed that on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common.
  • So, let's consider this rumor in earnest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NBA teams are remarkably diligent. They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected. Still, every now and then, a truly bizarre nugget hits the rumor mill and forces us to consider what exactly a team is thinking.

It has been revealed that on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common. Teams will do due diligence on a wide variety of players leading up to transaction periods in order to make sure they've covered their bases, and Begley gives no indication that there have even been talks between the Jazz and the Dallas Mavericks. Still, as he notes, "you're not gonna spend a lot of time on a player if you don't have any interest in him, so the idea of Utah spending some time internally on Kyrie Irving was interesting.".

So, let's consider this rumor in earnest. The Jazz entered this season with playoff expectations after four straight years in the lottery. They are 3-13 due to a combination of injuries, players adjusting to a new roster and simply poor performance. Utah has shown a willingness to trade for players outside of its perceived timeline before. The Jazz looked at then-33-year-old Jrue Holiday early in their rebuild in 2023, for instance, but backed off when Holiday's camp reportedly made it clear he would not be interested in extending.

Recent findings suggest that irving, still a star-caliber scorer, has the Mavericks at 8-7 through 15 games. He's averaging over 22 points on roughly his standard efficiency for a Dallas team with pretty limited shooting around him. We can't say at this stage whether or not the Mavericks are willing to trade him. The notion that they might depends on the team's asset deficit (Dallas does not control its own first-round pick again until 2031) and the 15-year age gap between Irving and franchise player Cooper Flagg, but Dallas could easily elect to simply build off this early success.

If they do take the long view and consider trade offers, Irving could absolutely help a team trying to win right now. Plenty of teams potentially looking for individual shot-creation, like the Detroit Pistons, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat, could be planning pursuits of the future Hall of Famer.

In a recent development, the question here is why the Jazz, specifically, would be interested in Irving, because on paper, there is perhaps not a single, high-profile player who makes less sense for this roster than he does. Utah's young core revolves around three perimeter players: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. The Jazz are so strong on that front that Bailey came off the bench to start the season, and it's unclear how exactly they initiative to handle their starting five when Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. return from injuries. If Utah isn't comfortable with Jackson playing center full time, and the Memphis Grizzlies certainly weren't, then one of those five players either needs to get traded or come off the bench.

In a recent development, adding Irving to this logjam doesn't make sense. Neither does trading one of those players for Irving. George is 23. Bailey is 20. Peterson is 19. Teams that are 10 games below .500 simply don't trade foundational pieces for players a decade or more their senior. They gave up three first-round picks for Jackson largely to improve their defense, and now that Walker Kessler plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, his presence matters more than ever.

Markkanen is the obvious trade candidate of the group, but he's still five years younger than Irving and plays a less saturated position. If Utah viewed Markkanen's max contract as a negative it needed to escape, that would be one thing, but there's just no evidence at this stage that this is the case. They have rebuffed trade interest in Markkanen at every turn. If Dallas were willing to put substantial draft equity on the table to cover the age and positional gaps here, there could perhaps be a conversation, but Dallas isn't in a position to do so.

There's some merit to the idea that Utah might eventually want to shake up its backcourt. There were rumors during the draft process that Peterson's representatives were skeptical of Utah as a landing spot because they also represent George and felt that two score-first guards would clash. Even if the Jazz were prepared to split them up less than 20 games into Peterson's career, Irving himself has typically fared far better when he has been paired with a high-level passer. He won his championship with LeBron James. He's thriving next to Cooper Flagg now. His best trait is, and always has been, his scoring.

Industry observers note that and then, of course, there is the history shared between Irving and Utah's top executive. The CEO of the Jazz is Danny Ainge, who once traded for Irving when he ran the Boston Celtics. Before his second season in Boston, Irving publicly shared plans to re-sign with the Celtics as a free agent in 2019. When the time came, he instead joined the Brooklyn Nets, a divisional opponent. This is the NBA. If LeBron James can reunite with Dan Gilbert, any player-executive reunion is theoretically possible. Nonetheless, Ainge and Irving would seemingly be among the unlikeliest pairings in all of basketball. Put all of this together and this is a puzzling rumor to say the least.

Sometimes a rumor notes more about a team's big-picture aims than it does a specific target. For a variety of reasons, some of which we've covered, it seems exceedingly unlikely that the Jazz are going to trade for Irving. However, they've invested the time in considering it, as Begley noted. That means something, even if it doesn't mean a trade is coming.

According to recent reports, the simplest read on this is that Utah is concerned enough about its short-term prospects that it is considering investing in win-now help despite its 3-13 start. That, in itself, makes sense. The Jazz don't control their own first-round pick this season. They have no incentive to lose, and while making the postseason despite starting the season 10 games under .500 is improbable, it just happened a year ago when the 4-14 Charlotte Hornets recovered promptly enough to reach the Play-In Tournament. The Jazz are 5.5 games out of the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference right now. If they get healthy in time and make the right addition, perhaps they could still make a real run at it.

According to recent reports, skepticism about the George-Peterson fit, for now, should be on the back burner. Though the two fared far better early on when they played separately, both, at least for now, have better net ratings and true shooting percentages in the minutes they've shared than the minutes they haven't. George's usage skyrockets when he plays without Peterson, but that's to be expected with Markkanen and Jackson out.

In a recent development, there may have been concern early in the season, and that might have been when Irving crossed Utah's mind. There may still be concerns down the line when the Jazz have had a longer sample size to evaluate the pairing with the rest of their roster. For now, though, it's simply too early to consider splitting up such a talented tandem, especially right as the team has actually started winning some games.

However, ball-handling behind them is a valid concern. Utah declined its fourth-year option on backup point guard and former first-round pick Isaiah Collier, and the offense has been 6.5 points per 100 possessions worse with him on the floor this season. Adding a veteran backup point guard, if only to ease Peterson's burden during the minutes George rests, would be sensible. Irving is obviously no backup, but as perhaps the most notable point guard theoretically on the market, it makes sense that the Jazz would at least broach the concept internally.

Sources indicate that ainge hasn't earned the nickname "Trader Danny" for nothing. His teams are almost always at the center of the trade market, and as last year's Jackson deal proved, he's as capable of a stunner as he's ever been. Irving would certainly qualify as one. We shouldn't expect it. It wouldn't really make sense based on what we know now. But in the post-Luka Dončić trade NBA, it would be hard to dismiss basically any rumor involving a player of this stature.

Victor Wembanyama has dunked so much he hurt his hand, so he came up with a unique solution: The 'shunk'

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (541 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line?
  • According to recent reports, let's set the stage here.
  • According to recent reports, did Wemby just...
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

According to recent reports, let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

According to recent reports, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

It has been revealed that officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

That begs an vital question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

It has been revealed that wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

Industry observers note that fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no plans to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he stated after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

Damian Lillard stars in his Milwaukee return in another stark reminder of how bleak things are for the Bucks

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.
  • It has been revealed that bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores.
  • Lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.

It has been revealed that bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record.

Lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery.

Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he remarked, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt.".

Recent findings suggest that lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard said.

No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range.

It has been revealed that "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori remarked pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it.".

The moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then.

The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

Recent findings suggest that "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard said Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on.".

The desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury.

Recent findings suggest that five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference.

It has been revealed that and the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract.

No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks.

Just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a newly introduced promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the Memphis Grizzlies pounded the Golden State Warriors on Thursday to move to 12-4 on the year.
  • And then there's been everything in between.
  • So much has happened over the first month of the season that we're going to pause for a moment, take stock of what we've seen, and hand out a few bits of early hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Memphis Grizzlies pounded the Golden State Warriors on Thursday to move to 12-4 on the year. The Grizzlies were a popular pick to surprise some folks this year, but nobody saw this coming. On the other hand, Luka Dončić and Victor Wembanyama are lording over the league like castles on a hill, and that wasn't so hard to predict.

And then there's been everything in between. All the injuries, perhaps most notably. The Raptors and Pacers entered the season being hyped as new-look contenders, but so far Tyrese Haliburton and Kawhi Leonard have combined to play six games. The Warriors went from an eight-game winning streak to the Washington Generals with one Stephen Curry abdominal tweak. The 76ers can't lose a clutch game in a maze. Paul George has been reborn in Boston. The Rockets are flying. The Heat are getting hot. The Knicks' fog is lifting. It feels like Damian Lillard never left the Blazers. This rookie class looks potentially historic.

So much has happened over the first month of the season that we're going to pause for a moment, take stock of what we've seen, and hand out a few bits of early hardware. Who's been the MVP so far? What about the best rookie? What has been the biggest surprise? Biggest disappointment? In light of what we've seen so far, is anyone ready to change their preseason Finals pick? Our staff took a collective shot at tackling these topics below.

Botkin: It's a two-horse race so far and nobody is going to argue much with either pick, but I'm going with Luka. I thought the Lakers would be good (their over/under 46.5 win total was way too low), but not tied-for-the-best-record-in-the-league good. Likewise, we all knew Luka would score huge, but not damn-near 40 PPG huge. Throw in north of seven assists and seven rebounds and almost two steals a night, and the numbers are simply too overwhelming to deny.

Gonzalez: This is really tough. Luka Dončić has been playing some of the best basketball of his career, and he's a huge reason why the Lakers are down as my major surprise over the first month of the season. But for as good as Luka has been, Wemby's two-way dominance gives him the edge here. Wembanyama had the second 50-point game of his career against the Mavs, and he's averaging a 28-point double-double on 53% shooting from the field. He's also blocking an outrageous 4.1 shots per game and averaging more than a steal per outing. There's no answer for him at either end of the floor.

Recent findings suggest that kalland: Wemby's been awesome but for the first month it's gotta be Luka. He's averaging 38 points per game on 47/38/86 splits! The Lakers are 13-3 in spite of defensive concerns, and it's because Dončić is out of his mind. What's amazing is he's going to have to keep up this ridiculous pace to win MVP and for the Lakers to remain at the top of the West. I'm excited to see how long he can maintain this level.

Maloney: I won't argue with anyone who picks Luka Dončić when he's averaging nearly 40 points per game, but I'm going with Wembanyama because of his two-way dominance. He's third in scoring, fourth in rebounding and first in blocks by a significant margin. The 1.7 blocks-per-game gap between Wembanyama (3.9) and Donovan Clingan (2.2), who sits in second, is as massive as the gap between Clingan and Dean Wade (0.5), who ranks 102nd in the league. In 483 minutes with Wembanyama on the floor this season, the Spurs have a 98.7 defensive rating; in 290 minutes without him, they have a 123.4 defensive rating. Overall, Wembanyama has an unfathomable +41.5 net rating differential.

Sources indicate that quinn: Dončić is flirting with 40 points per game. He's leading the NBA in both 3-point attempts and free throws. He's the undisputed engine of the NBA's best offense, one that dies whenever he rests. The Lakers have the NBA's best record because Luka Dončić is on their team. That's it. They're average at basically everything else: rebounding, defense, you name it. But their offense dominates because he is on their team. Victor Wembanyama has much more to work with around him. No one else is even in their galaxy, though Stephen Curry might've had a case had he stayed healthy.

Salerno: I've been pleasantly surprised with the Lakers so far. The pieces are working together nicely. However, the Lakers obviously wouldn't obvousuly be this good without Dončić, who is somehow taking his game to an entirely newly introduced level. He's on a mission to win MVP. He's been the best player in the league for the first month of the season. I think this will be the year he finally wins the award.

In a recent development, botkin: I actually think Darius Acuff's numbers are actually too good in the sense that voters can't fathom a rookie averaging 26 and 7 without it being some fishy gimmick. It's not a gimmick. He just has total control of an NBA offense, which would make any player's numbers go up, Luka Dončić included. That said, Lendeborg has been better as both a real go-to player on a real team and from a scoring efficiency standpoint. The honeymoon has been heavily interrupted with Stephen Curry's injury as the Warriors look, well, like the Kings. But as of now Lendeborg deserves the award. Long term, I'm really watching Darryn Peterson as Utah's season quickly circles the drain. His numbers are rising quickly, and it may not be long before his development becomes Utah's undisputed top priority.

Gonzalez: Lendeborg picked a fight with Luka in his very first game as a pro, trash-talked while guarding the Lakers superstar, then stated he lost all respect for him afterward. He stepped into the starting lineup and immediately looked like he belonged for an injury-plagued Warriors team that sorely needed his presence. And he was so unnerved by a blowout loss to the Spurs that he chopped off his hair, leaving Steve Kerr to tell the media "apparently that's his response to getting beat by 40, is to go right to the barber." His personality alone wins him the award. The numbers are good, too.

Recent findings suggest that kalland: This rookie class has lived up to the hype so far, but right now I have to give the edge to the Warriors rookie sensation. Lendeborg came into the league talking that talk, and while he's put his foot in his mouth here and there, he's largely walked the walk to back it up. What separates him from the likes of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer presently is his combination of productivity and efficiency. But we've already seen that take a dip without Stephen Curry so there is certainly an opportunity for others to make up ground as the Warriors struggle without their top star.

Industry observers note that maloney: Lendeborg has started to fade a bit, and so have the Warriors since Steph Curry went down with an oblique injury, but the No. 11 pick has still done enough to earn the nod ahead of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer. Everyone liked the Lendeborg pick for the Warriors, but no one expected this. He's come in and immediately established himself as their second-best player while doing a little bit of everything. He's second among rookies in scoring, second in rebounding, fifth in assists and tied for fourth in steals, all while shooting 37.2% from 3-point range.

Quinn: Cameron Boozer is probably trending toward winning. His 3-point shooting is coming around, his interior scoring is progressing, and he does all of the little things everyone promised. Darius Acuff has the biggest numbers, but they're fake. Not fake in the empty calories sense, but fake in that all of the other rookies are being asked to play roles on real basketball teams, whereas Sacramento has elected to devote its entire season to Acuff's development by letting him do basically whatever he wants. If we're simply naming the best rookie thus far this season, though, the answer is obviously Yaxel Lendeborg. Things have gotten harder with Stephen Curry sidelined, but Lendeborg has resuscitated Golden State's postseason ambitions. He's scoring efficiently, shouldering an enormous defensive load and has fit into a system that is notoriously tricky for the wrong kinds of players. Boozer may get there by the end of the season, but for now, this is Yaxel's trophy.

Salerno: In my rookie rankings released earlier this week, I had Yaxel Lendeborg No. 1. However, I would give strong consideration to Acuff because he is being asked to do more than any other rookie in his class. He is putting up elite numbers on a very bad Kings team that would be even worse if he wasn't in the lineup. I don't think you can go wrong with any of the top contenders. Darryn Peterson has also played very well as of late and will end up being in the mix down the stretch.

Botkin: So many good options here. Obviously the Grizzlies, who are probably the correct answer. I certainly didn't foresee Minnesota holding this tightly to the rope without Anthony Edwards. But I'm going with the 76ers, who felt like a team that was going to take a while to figure things out but instead are out to a 13-3 record. There are some qualifiers. A perfect 11-0 mark in clutch games is unsustainable, and they can't keep digging themselves into holes (six comeback wins from at least 10 down). But the bottom line is this is a team that looks like it has played together for far longer than it has. The roles clarified almost immediately. Joel Embiid hasn't gotten hurt yet. There's a mental toughness to this team that I suppose makes sense given the individual players we're talking about, but collectively this thing is way more tied together than I thought possible this early in the season.

Gonzalez: There weren't many people outside of Los Angeles who predicted the Lakers would be atop the Western Conference a month into the season. There might not have been that many inside Los Angeles either. The skepticism can be forgiven considering the Lakers bid goodbye to arguably the greatest player of all time during the summer, then overhauled a large portion of the roster. In came Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Matisse Thybulle, among others. After the reconstruction, head coach JJ Redick mentioned that for the first time in his tenure "the pieces actually fit together." That's been the case so far on the offensive end. The Lakers are first in points per game and third in offensive rating. It definitely helps that Luka Dončić is playing some of the best basketball of his career and leading the league in scoring by a wide margin. While Dončić battles Victor Wembanyama for MVP frontrunner status, his Lakers are in a race with the Spurs for the top slot in the West. The former isn't much of a surprise, but the latter certainly is.

Kalland: Yes, the Grizzlies have faced a very generous schedule through the first month of the season, but even with that context, no one predicted a 12-4 start with Ty Jerome hanging out among the league's leading scorers. Cam Boozer's a strong ROY candidate (and is slowly improving his shooting efficiency) and the Grizzlies just keep finding diamonds in the rough to maintain competitiveness. They've got eight guys averaging 10+ points per game and are top 10 in offensive and defensive rating. Reality may arrive soon, but even so, this hot start has given them a great chance at emerging as a Play-In squad in the West.

According to recent reports, maloney: The NBA intellegencia was high on the Grizzlies coming into the season, but in the sense that they would surpass their win total projection and make a run at the Play-In Tournament. Instead, they've jumped out to a 12-4 start, which has them in fourth place in the Western Conference and is good for the fifth-best record in the league. They lead the league in offensive rating (121.2) and are third in net rating (+9.9) behind only the Spurs and the Celtics. Even though they've had the easiest schedule in the league thus far, this is still remarkable.

Quinn: For four games with Anthony Edwards, the Timberwolves looked like the NBA's best offense. Then their best player got hurt ... and they became the NBA's best defense. They're hardly slouching as scorers either. LaMelo Ball's playmaking has facilitated breakout years for Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu. Jonathan Kuminga is making 3s and defending like the Warriors always wanted him to. Minnesota's transition from moodiness to giddiness is palpable whenever they play, and when they get Edwards back, they're going to be terrifying.

It has been revealed that salerno: Here is a wild stat for you: Cameron Boozer has a 159-21 record across games in high school, college and the NBA (during the first month of the season). He is the ultimate winner who elevates his respective teams to greater heights. Between Boozer being firmly in the Rookie of the Year race and Ty Jerome making a case as the Most Improved Player, the Grizzlies have been quite entertaining to watch. Memphis has pushed the right buttons.

Botkin: I'm probably a little biased on this one. I'm a lifelong Warriors fan and figured they would stink this year, but I allowed myself to get my hopes up with the way the team came out of the gate. I should've known better. As soon as Curry went down, which was probably inevitable, the Warriors turned into one of the worst teams in the league. It's a complete bummer. Hopefully he won't be out too much longer, and the Warriors can pick back up where he left off, but this is just a harsh reminder of how thin the margin is for this team, and it's just not likely to go their way over the long haul. If I was born in Indiana, I would say the same thing about Tyrese Haliburton's injury. Same goes for the Toronto fans with Kawhi only managing two games so far. All the injuries stink. But Curry's has hit the hardest.

According to recent reports, gonzalez: Moving to the 3-2-1 system was unnecessary. The league overcorrected for last year's perfect tanking storm and didn't account for a simple truth of basketball: sometimes teams are just bad. No amount of tinkering is going to stop that. More than half the teams in the East are under .500. The West has four more such teams, bringing the total league-wide to 12. Adam Silver didn't want to incentivize tanking, but by putting too much of the league's thumb on the scale, they've made it harder on the worst teams to get better. Not to mention that the odd entertainment value of fans checking their lottery odds in the tank wars sideshow has been somewhat stripped away. [Stands up and repeats himself yet again] Tanking wasn't actually a problem.

Recent findings suggest that kalland: The injuries so far this season have been brutal. Just about every team you'd point to as a disappointment -- Utah, Indiana, Toronto -- can point to injuries as a major reason for their early struggles. The frustrating thing is there's not an easy solve to the injury glitch (schedule length is hard to blame for injuries in the first month) and every year it feels like we're playing injury roulette to determine who can and can't be a contender. The wheel started spinning earlier than usual in 2026-27.

Maloney: I'm going with Robby here. The absurd amount of injuries, coupled with who is getting injured, has been the story of the season so far. You could form an All-Star team with all of the guys who have gone down with multi-week ailments: Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Haliburton, Paolo Banchero, Kawhi Leonard, Stephen Curry, Austin Reaves, Dylan Harper, Jalen Duren, Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., Kon Knueppel, Ja Morant, Caleb Wilson, Cason Wallace.

Quinn: Look, we knew Charlotte was taking a step back when the team traded LaMelo Ball. The Hornets have been plagued by injuries all season. Some of this can be explained. Fine. Their offense still makes me want to vomit. No team turns the ball over more often. No team shoots less efficiently. No team is forced to take more shots in the last four seconds of the shot clock. No team leaves you feeling as though you're watching a panicked 14-year-old try to play minutes for the varsity squad more often. I had very high hopes for No. 1 option Brandon Miller. I trusted the system Charles Lee built last season. I figured they'd be worse, but still respectable, because this organization has displayed a genuine, systemic competence over the past few years. I think that will win out in the end. For now, I pity the poor souls in Charlotte buying tickets to these games, because they're quite nearly unwatchable.

Salerno: Yes, Utah has been bad this season, largely due to the injury bug, but I was bullish on this team heading into the season. I had Utah finishing sixth in the West and making the playoffs outright. Instead, Utah is heading toward the lottery again, where it doesn't even own its own first-round pick in what should end up being a lackluster draft. The organization's top priority for the remainder of the season is developing Darryn Peterson.

Botkin: Spurs over Knicks. The Spurs are the clear Western Conference favorite with all the OKC injuries. The Wolves, Lakers and Rockets deserve to be in the conversation, but they're all second-paragraph entries. It's the Spurs until they get hit with some major injury, too, but let's not jinx it. In the East, I could make a case for four teams. The 76ers have the late-game goods and individual creation that is exponentially impactful in the postseason. The Celtics look incredible with Paul George flourishing. The Pistons are just flat-out tough and they've been doing it without Jalen Duren. But I'm still picking the Knicks, who are starting to come out of their fog. They are so perfectly built for the playoffs, and remember, they weren't a great regular-season team last year, either.

Gonzalez: Spurs over Celtics. After losing their first two games to start the season, the Spurs look every bit as good as they did during last season's run to the finals -- if not better. The three-guard starting unit hasn't slowed them down at all, and Wemby has been unreal at both ends of the floor. And while the Celtics took a lot of heat in the immediate aftermath of the Jaylen Brown for Paul George trade, we all should have known that they would still be among the best teams in the East this season. Both franchises are smart and steady. Meeting this summer would make for an excellent Finals.

Kalland: Spurs over Celtics. I have to stick with my preseason Finals prediction because it's not every year a preseason pick still looks that good a month in. The Spurs look like a juggernaut, and their top competitor in the West, the OKC Thunder, will once again (likely) be without Jalen Williams for the playoffs. We'll see what the Timberwolves look like when Anthony Edwards returns, but for now it still feels like San Antonio and everyone else. In the East, I felt good about this Celtics team entering the season, and nothing has changed my belief they have what it takes to win the conference.

According to recent reports, maloney: Spurs over Celtics. I picked Thunder over Celtics ahead of the season, in large part because of how difficult it has been for teams to get back to the Finals in consecutive seasons during this parity era. But now that the Thunder have been decimated with injuries, the Spurs have what appears to be a clear path through the West. I'll stick with the Celtics in the East, which has not been anywhere near as good as we expected this season.

Quinn: Spurs over Knicks. Oklahoma City's injuries are really all that's changed to me. I don't think the Lakers have the defense or frontcourt depth to win three straight series in the West. I don't think the Rockets will be able to create good enough shots. I need to see Ball prove it in a playoff setting before I trust Minnesota. The star-studded 76ers have thus far been clutch merchants. The underlying numbers are lower on them than their record suggests. The opposite is true for Boston, who is blowing everyone out of the gym, but is going to have issues creating shots off of the dribble in the playoffs and defending man-to-man against the best offenses. I have an eyebrow quirked at Indiana and Toronto when they get their best players back. I'll reengage with the Thunder if and when they cash in some of their trade chips. For now, though, nothing has convinced me that last year's finalists are going to be dethroned. The Knicks and Spurs are the most complete teams in their respective conferences, and I'd expect San Antonio to learn from last June's defeat in a revenge series this time around.

Champions League Final: What the Future of Football Looks Like – MH

📅 01 Jun 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 01.06.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Opinion mit 1 Kommentar.
  • Industry observers note that which ideology will shape the football of the future?
  • Under manager Arteta, Arsenal have focused this season on perfecting defending in a low block.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 01.06.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Opinion mit 1 Kommentar.

Industry observers note that which ideology will shape the football of the future? The 2026 Champions League final was supposed to provide answers to this question. After all, FC Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain had reached the final, two teams whose playing philosophies could hardly seem more different at first glance.

Under manager Arteta, Arsenal have focused this season on perfecting defending in a low block. This works so effectively in part because Arsenal combine low block defending with very high, aggressive, man oriented pressing. The combination of these two defensive styles also ensures that Arsenal’s opponents cannot adapt to just one form of defending. In attack, meanwhile, set pieces have been Arsenal’s primary source of goal threat this season. Statistics, such as their newly established record for goals from corners in a Premier League season, demonstrate this impressively.

Sources indicate that while positional play has shaped football over the past fifteen years, it is becoming increasingly apparent that teams are neutralising the positional advantages of their opponents. The growing importance of large analytical staffs has certainly contributed to this development. These teams observe opponents’ adjustments in real time during matches and immediately relay their findings to the coaching staff.

This is precisely where Arsenal’s low block defending comes into play. It is designed to deny the opponent any positional advantages whatsoever. With Mikel Arteta, the former assistant coach of Pep Guardiola, positional play is, in a sense, being reimagined from a defensive perspective. Arsenal are regarded as one of the best examples of the systematic elimination of opponents’ positional advantages. As already suggested, this trend is not limited to the London club. It can be observed across virtually all of Europe’s top leagues. Only rarely are teams now able to generate sustained positional advantages over extended periods, such as numerical superiorities or free players.

An example of Manchester City exploiting a positional advantage – from “How Guardiola’s 3-2-2-3 Ultimately Solves Defensive Play”.

Industry observers note that the most offensively successful teams in Europe are no longer distinguished by creating chances from positional advantages controlled by the coach. Although Paris, under coach Enrique, who also comes from the school of positional play, fundamentally pursues a positional style, chances are not created solely through positional advantages. The two other most offensively successful teams in Europe, Barcelona and Bayern Munich, likewise no longer rely on purely positional attacking play. In particular, the highly successful Barcelona side mainly display typical relationist patterns in possession that are no longer based on the classical positions.

The exemplary execution of an attacking move without classical positions – from “Barça’s 174 Goals: How Flick Built Europe’s Best Attack”.

Industry observers note that it is remarkable how much significance is regularly attached to the Champions League final when discussing what the future of football will look like. Ironically, the Champions League is a competition whose format makes it comparatively susceptible to randomness and short term fluctuations. After all, the champion among Europe’s best 24 teams is not determined through a league system over a large number of matches, but through a knockout format in which individual games, or even individual moments within games, can have enormous consequences. The smaller the sample size and the greater the importance of individual matches, the larger the influence of chance becomes.

It has been revealed that from the perspective of forecasting, this is a fundamental principle. Future developments should not be predicted on the basis of isolated events, but on recurring observations. A single match, even a Champions League final, provides only an extremely limited data set. It may offer indications of existing trends, but it is hardly suitable as proof of a future development. In forecasting research, this is referred to as the danger of assigning disproportionate significance to extraordinary or sensational events and drawing far reaching conclusions from them. This tendency can be observed regularly in football, and particularly in this context.

In a recent development, attempting to determine the future of football solely on the basis of a Champions League final would therefore be a serious misjudgment, regardless of how dominant or spectacular the winner may appear. Developments that can be observed across many matches, different competitions, and multiple teams are far more informative. Only when certain aspects repeatedly prevail under different conditions can they be regarded as robust trends.

It is therefore all the more surprising that many coaches and clubs nevertheless tend to interpret individual matches at the highest level as blueprints for the future. This often leads to a kind of tactical overreaction: a team wins a prestigious competition with a particular approach, after which numerous imitators attempt to copy its superficial characteristics. Anyone seeking to understand the future of the game should focus less on the result of a final and more on the underlying trends that emerge across a broader body of evidence. Fortunately, this year’s Champions League final did not produce a clear winner (and especially not Arsenal!).

A more robust foundation would, for example, be the analysis of the championship winning teams in Europe’s top leagues. International performance should only be considered as a supplementary indicator because of the increased degree of random variability involved. In this context, Arsenal, Bayern, Paris, and Barcelona deserve particular attention.

“Formidables v Expendables? PSG v Arsenal could be a classic” – The Guardian.

“PSG Meets Arsenal: A Final of Contrasts and Milestones” – NeunzigPlus.

“Attacking Football Wins [After a Penalty Shootout]” – 11 Freunde.

It has been revealed that “Attacking Spectacle Meets Defensive Fortress” – Die Welt: “PSG vs. Arsenal: Title Defence or Historic Coronation?”.

Recent findings suggest that many analyses before and after the Champions League final contrast two opposing football ideologies. This is often accompanied by the assumption that the respective styles of play fundamentally contradict one another and cannot be reconciled. According to the implicit logic, the winner of the match would determine which approach will shape the future of football. Will we see spectacular attacking football with a multitude of goals in the future, or an increasingly “pragmatic”, defensively oriented game? Following this interpretation, the final should have provided an answer to that question had the result been different.

Industry observers note that in reality, however, with regard to the future development of football, this is merely an apparent contrast between two ideas that only at first glance seem hardly more different. On the one hand stands the perfection of low block defending, on the other a style of attacking play that is less oriented around positions. These approaches are by no means mutually exclusive. In fact, they can be combined exceptionally well.

Strictly speaking, Arsenal already provide an example of a team that has successfully combined two supposedly contradictory dogmas. There, phases of deep defending in a low block alternate with aggressive, man oriented pressing. Who would have thought 15 years ago that a team could simultaneously be one of the best pressing sides in Europe and still defend deep on a regular basis?

According to recent reports, high man marking pressing currently unites almost all successful (and unsuccessful) teams in Europe. It removes positional advantages from the opponent, places them under constant pressure so that they cannot establish control through possession, and has therefore become a particularly effective defensive tool. At the same time, it seems entirely logical that, with the growing spread of less position bound possession strategies, the current principles of man marking will also have to evolve.

If any prediction for the future of elite football can be derived from the Champions League final, it is that success will not depend on individual, seemingly distinct ideologies, but rather on the combination of elements from the best teams, adapted to the strengths of the players available. The ability to defend both compactly in a deep block and with maximum intensity in a high press will be just as indispensable as an attacking game that does not depend on finding large spaces in the opposition’s structure. The most successful teams of the future will be those capable of combining these different modes of play.

For precisely this reason, we should be cautious about predicting the future of football based on today’s ideologies. The categories of football tactics are ultimately only provisional descriptions of our current understanding of the game. Particularly revealing are developments that break apparent rules. They show where our models reach their limits and where upcoming tactical possibilities emerge. A prime example of this is the development of relationism, which challenges many assumptions underlying the European possession based game, positional play, and offers solutions in the tightest of spaces. The future of football will therefore most likely not lie within existing, rigid schools of thought, but rather where their boundaries are transcended.

Sources indicate that “I think today we saw a lot of good, intense defending. The distances are just so, so small. And you only have two options. The first is: go all in. The second is: drop completely. The space in between doesn’t work against players of [PSG’s] level, and it doesn’t work against players of our level either.” — Vincent Kompany after the first leg against Paris in the Champions League semi final.

It seems entirely logical that defending in elite football will increasingly concentrate on two extremes in the near future. On the one hand, there is aggressive high pressing, which aims to deprive the opponent of time and control in possession. On the other hand, there is particularly deep defending in a compact block, designed to prevent high quality chances against positional teams.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, the more varied a style of play is, the more difficult it becomes for opponents to prepare for it. The more closely teams resemble one another in their principles, the easier it becomes to identify recurring patterns and target them specifically. The history of football tactics is shaped by precisely such developments. Dominant ideas provoke counterreactions. Positional play, for example, only came under pressure through newly introduced forms of man marking defending.

According to recent reports, if, in the future, almost all teams rely on the same defensive solutions, upcoming attacking strategies will eventually be developed to counter them as well. For this reason alone, it seems unlikely that the entire future of defending will lie exclusively in the two extremes of man marking pressing and space oriented deep blocks. Teams will continue to search for ways to confront opponents with different attacking and defensive concepts and thereby present them with constantly changing challenges. It is precisely when tactical approaches become too widespread and therefore familiar to teams that the conditions for successful innovation emerge.

What will the football of the future look like? Neither will a single at the moment dominant ideology shape the future of football, nor can a single Champions League final reliably provide insight into the game’s long term development, regardless of how it ends.

What remains is the hope that coaches and analysts will become somewhat more creative in the future. Rather than searching for answers about the future of the game (or their own teams) in Europe’s biggest match, they should focus more on developing fresh solutions and questioning established assumptions. The next major innovation in football tactics will most likely not emerge from the confirmation of existing ideologies.
