Latest Update: Timberwolves, Grizzlies reportedly hope to move to Eastern Conference after expansion; who makes more sense?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1446 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two upcoming teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30.
  • Recent findings suggest that several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic.
  • Sources indicate that getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two upcoming teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30. Perhaps the biggest is geographic. Both Seattle and Las Vegas are located firmly in the western half of the United States. Should those cities eventually be granted teams, they would play in the Western Conference, leaving the league with unbalanced conferences. Therefore, someone in the West would have to move to the East in order to balance the conferences at 16 teams apiece.

Recent findings suggest that several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic. While the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans are not out of the running, the likeliest teams to move in realignment, for now, are reportedly the Minnesota Timberwolves and Memphis Grizzlies.

Sources indicate that getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels. Of course, there are obvious basketball reasons for preferring the East. Putting aside the decades of Western Conference superiority that hold little weight in the long run, the two teams best positioned to succeed over the next decade or so are the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder. As the Fresh York Knicks learned last June, the easiest path to a championship is avoiding Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander until they've already spent seven games battling each other.

Recent findings suggest that but this isn't just a basketball conversation. The NBA, like most major American professional sports leagues, tilts east. There are simply more major cities in the Eastern half of the country than the Western half. Of the league's 30 existing teams, 17 play east of the Mississippi River: the 15 already in the Eastern Conference, along with the Timberwolves and Grizzlies.

Travel is simply easier playing in the East. One projection of how many total miles each NBA team will travel this season has only the Miami Heat in the top half of the league, with the other 14 slots belonging to Western Conference teams. That projection has the Heat crossing 24 time zones, while every Western Conference team crosses at least 36.

So Minnesota, Memphis and Upcoming Orleans are all incentivized to move, and with the Grizzlies and Timberwolves seemingly favored, let's evaluate the cases for each.

Industry observers note that the fundamental case for the Grizzlies is geographic. Memphis is further East than Minneapolis. As The Athletic points out, it is closer to more Eastern Conference teams as well, as it is within 600 miles of five East teams (Charlotte Hornets, Atlanta Hawks, Indiana Pacers, Chicago Bulls and Milwaukee Bucks). This not only makes travel easier for the Grizzlies, but for those teams as well.

While the Timberwolves are considered the better team right now, Memphis is probably the team better positioned to be competitive in the long run. Minnesota's best players -- Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu -- are all in their mid-20s earning market-rate salaries, and Rudy Gobert is much older at 34. Plus, the Timberwolves are essentially devoid of first-round draft capital.

In a recent development, the Grizzlies have a significant draft surplus, and their best players -- Cameron Boozer, Cedric Coward and Zach Edey -- are still on their rookie deals. If the idea is balancing the two conferences competitively, even if the Timberwolves have a higher immediate upside, the Grizzlies are probably the team we should expect to contend longer.

And then there's the matter of maintaining established rivalries. While neither the Grizzlies nor the Timberwolves are franchises steeped in historical success, Minnesota's last few years have established the Timberwolves as genuine postseason rivals to several notable Western Conference teams. They've faced Nikola Jokiċ and the Denver Nuggets in multiple recent playoff series. They've faced Luka Dončić in multiple recent playoff series, even if they've come against different teams. Their series against the Spurs last spring included a Wembanyama ejection.

Recent findings suggest that the NBA may prefer to maximize the number of games Edwards plays against these high-profile opponents because there are existing narratives surrounding those matchups. In that case, keeping the Timberwolves in the West makes sense while allowing the Grizzlies to shift to the East.

In a recent development, minnesota's geographic case is a bit more nuanced. While Memphis is closer to more teams, Minnesota is closer to a few geographically convenient ones. If we assume for the moment that the upcoming, 16-team conferences are going to come with four divisions featuring four teams each, Minnesota's proximity to Milwaukee, Chicago and Indiana makes for an easy four-team pod.

Sources indicate that the rest of the conference becomes remarkably easy to group from there. We have three more roughly Midwestern teams (Cleveland, Toronto and Detroit), five in the Northeast (New York, Brooklyn, Boston, Philadelphia and Washington) and four in the Southeast (Charlotte, Miami, Orlando and Atlanta). Just move one of those Northeastern teams to the Midwestern group -- presumably Washington, as it doesn't play in the existing Atlantic Division -- and you're set. If the NBA wants to make divisions a more prominent part of scheduling moving forward, Minnesota makes doing so much easier.

Sources indicate that there's also the idea of giving Edwards, one of the league's more personable stars, an easier path to the NBA Finals by getting him away from Wembanyama and Gilgeous-Alexander. The NBA is, ultimately, a star business, and if stacking the deck in Edwards' favor helps build him up as one of the faces of the league, there is obvious appeal in doing so.

By all accounts, we are far closer to resolution on a Las Vegas team than to the return of the Sonics in Seattle. Bidding has seemingly been more robust in Las Vegas, and an announcement is expected in the near future. If an announcement on Vegas comes before one in Seattle, there will be a brief period in which the NBA has an odd number of planned franchises.

Sources indicate that that does not mean that it will ever actually play a season with only 31 teams. Seattle, as commissioner Adam Silver has described, is much more of a turnkey operation than Las Vegas because of its arena situation and preexisting basketball history. In theory, a Seattle team could be revealed much later than a Las Vegas team and still begin play in the same season. For now, the reported target for expansion teams to tip off is the 2028-29 season. However, if Seattle's bidding process takes too long for the two to begin play at the same time, or worse, if no Seattle group manages to put forth an acceptable bid in the near future, the possibility of one or even multiple seasons with 31 teams rather than the expected 32 probably does exist.

The NBA -- and every other major American professional sports league -- has had unbalanced conferences in the past. None do now. It creates scheduling headaches, and it's just blatantly unfair. Forcing some teams to overcome 15 opponents to reach the Finals while others only have to top 14 makes playing in the smaller conference too much of an advantage, and since the conference presently believed to be the superior one (the West) would be getting the Las Vegas team, competitive balance would go from a problem to an outright crisis.

Fans have been calling for the abolition of conferences for decades now. Getting it to actually pass a vote would be harder. Realignment is voted on by the board of governors, so abolishing the conferences theoretically would be as well. Eastern Conference owners love having an easier path to the playoffs and the gate revenue those postseason games generate. This is where the idea of a season or two with just 31 teams in the league carries some appeal. It could give the NBA an opportunity to test the abolition of conferences provisionally with the idea that conferences would return when the league reaches 32 unless a upcoming vote determines otherwise.

The appeal of removing conferences altogether stems from the inherent fairness of a playoff system determined solely by record. There have been concerns about how removing the geographic component of playoff scheduling would affect travel, but there are potential solutions there. Returning to the "2-3-2" home-court format would minimize travel, or higher seeds could be allowed to select opponents in the early rounds to decide for themselves how they'd like to prioritize travel. The odds are obviously against the removal of conferences altogether, but expansion offers a potential opportunity to test it without committing to it long-term, and that's an opportunity the NBA would be foolish not to at least explore.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end.
  • Industry observers note that the 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end. The 49ers have released Aiyuk, who will now look to continue his career with a upcoming team, according to a report from ESPN.

Industry observers note that the 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9. With that exemption ending on Nov. 23, the 49ers elected to move on from Aiyuk, who hasn't played an NFL game since tearing his ACL and MCL during the 2024 season. Aiyuk had signed a four-year, $120 deal with the 49ers that offseason following a tumultuous negotiation. That contract, as right now structured, still has two years remaining, with a 2027 cap hit of $40.5 million according to Over the Cap, meaning Aiyuk will likely need to clear waivers before any team formally signs him.

Sources indicate that aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list. That November, it was reported that the 49ers voided the guaranteed money in his contract for 2026 due to lack of participation. In December, the 49ers placed him on their reserve/left squad list.

This summer, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/did not report list (meaning the 49ers were not obligated to pay him and he did not count against their roster) after he did not report to training camp. Aiyuk had since applied for reinstatement with the NFL and was granted it earlier this month.

Before 2024, Aiyuk enjoyed a productive career with the 49ers, who selected him with the 25th overall pick in the 2020 draft. In 2022, he eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards for the first time and caught a career-high eight touchdowns. The following season, he recorded a career-high 1,342 receiving yards while helping the 49ers reach the Super Bowl.

While his recent actions in San Francisco might scare some teams off, Aiyuk will likely draw interest from teams that need help at receiver. Aiyuk has long been linked to the Commanders; he and Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels were teammates at Arizona State. The Steelers are another team that could potentially be a landing spot for Aiyuk.

Sources indicate that despite not having Aiyuk, the 49ers are 9-1 and would be the No. 1 seed in the NFL if the playoffs started today.

Tech Report: Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The big prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.
  • The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.
  • According to recent reports, let's stop right there.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The big prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.

The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

According to recent reports, let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the Mets are getting a surefire ace for nearly a decade.

Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

Since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

The recent track record here notes this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

According to recent reports, there isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

Industry observers note that he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

Industry observers note that we'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

According to recent reports, I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. His nine-year deal means it'll run through his age-38 season.

Sources indicate that for those so worried about the long-term finances of the Cohen family, are you sure you're really worried that Skubal won't be productive through five, six or even all nine years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

It has been revealed that yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

According to recent reports, gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

Justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

David Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

Corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

It has been revealed that zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

According to recent reports, CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

Industry observers note that max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

In a recent development, we can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

It has been revealed that by this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

Are you sure a 9-year, $450 million deal for this guy is a "risk?".

I think we could argue that it'll be a bargain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Injuries have been one of the defining stories of the young 2026-27 NBA season, and while some teams like the Oklahoma City Thunder are unfortunately months away from relief, others are beginning to see a light at the end of the health tunnel. We're now nearly a month or so out from the early-season wave of losses, and on Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania gave updates on the health of several key absent players. Let's use that as a launching point to check in on a handful of injured stars.

Sources indicate that it took Indiana's star point guard a full season to recover from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, but sadly, his return lasted just four games before he headed back to the sideline. Haliburton was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain in October, and according to ESPN, he will be sidelined for at least the next couple of weeks.

For now, there is no firmer timeline than that, with Pacers coach Rick Carlisle saying in a recent radio interview that he didn't think it was "out of the question" that Haliburton would play in November, but he would not "put a hard date on anything.".

Haliburton looked mostly like himself in the four games he played early this season, averaging just under 22 points and 10 assists. The Pacers have fallen to 5-10 and the Eastern Conference's No. 10 seed without him, and they are seemingly aware of the need for reinforcements. The Pacers "clearly are looking at doing something" on the trade market, with an upgrade on the wing viewed as a strong possibility, Jake Fischer mentioned Friday on SiriusXM NBA Radio.

Industry observers note that A return to action seems further off for Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards, who had knee surgery in late October. Edwards spoke with reporters Thursday and remarked he has "no clue" when he'll be able to return to the floor and declined to offer a timetable, per ESPN.

In a recent development, edwards missed 21 games last year and dealt with a knee issue in the postseason. Despite a hot start, that included a 47-point outburst against the Cavaliers, Edwards continued to experience discomfort in the knee, prompting the team to choose the surgery route rather than have their superstar continue playing through pain.

"It needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple years," Edwards said. "But who knows? Maybe in a couple years I might have to get something else. But hopefully not. I think I'll be pretty good.".

Recent findings suggest that led by LaMelo Ball, the Wolves have excelled even in Edwards' absence. At 11-5, Minnesota sits at No. 5 in the Western Conference standings entering their game against the Grizzlies on Saturday.

According to recent reports, leonard has played just twice this season due to knee swelling, but according to Charania, there is optimism that he will return within the next few weeks. Leonard has been dealing with patellar tendinopathy, more commonly known as "jumper's knee," TSN reported on Tuesday. That is the same issue he dealt with throughout his 2019 championship season. SportsNet confirmed that reporting, while noting that swelling is not typically how that injury presents. SportsNet's reporting indicates that the swelling and jumper's knee are separate complications.

The good news on this front is that the reporting to this point indicates that the Raptors do not expect these issues to linger once Leonard returns. Toronto successfully managed Leonard's health through that title season, and is being cautious to start this year as well. However, his absence has certainly been felt as Toronto is in the midst of a six-game losing streak without him.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the player Leonard was traded for is just about ready to make his Clippers debut. Brandon Ingram is expected to return Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to Charania. Ingram suffered a partially torn Achilles tendon last season, which kept him out of the Clippers' lineup at the start of this year. His absence has been keenly felt in Los Angeles as the Clippers have scuttled to a 4-10 start without him. Los Angeles has both a bottom-eight offense and defense so far this season, so getting Ingram on the court should represent a helpful talent infusion.

San Antonio's second-year star thankfully avoided a major injury when he fell on the court against the Clippers on Thursday. He will, however, miss 1-3 weeks with a left hip rotator strain. Harper was walking without a limp following the injury, per The San Antonio Express-News, a positive sign for his recovery.

Industry observers note that the Spurs have the NBA's best record at 13-3, but the story to watch as Harper rests is the performance of former All-Star De'Aaron Fox. Just beginning a four-year max contract, Fox has scored just 23 points in his last three games combined. He's averaging the fewest points and assists of his career since his rookie season. The Spurs had been starting their three high-profile guards -- Fox, Harper and Stephon Castle -- together early in the season. It was working, but with the caveat that that group never played a second without Victor Wembanyama. The Spurs are more than 40 points per 100 possessions better when their MVP candidate is on the floor.

Industry observers note that if Fox can't right the ship while Harper is out, that could open the door to San Antonio moving him to the bench upon Harper's return. The Spurs thrived last season with two ball-handlers, two shooters and Wembanyama in their starting lineup. The three guards are working because basically anything works with Wembanyama, but when the competition gets stiffer in the playoffs, it's going to be harder to get away with so little shooting in the starting lineup. That puts the onus on Fox to prove he still belongs in the starting lineup, and bouncing back while Harper is out will be a substantial part of that.

#153398. Latest Update: Winners and losers of the Tarik Skubal signing: Blue Jays, Dodgers strike out; David Stearns looks nervous

Latest Update: Winners and losers of the Tarik Skubal signing: Blue Jays, Dodgers strike out; David Stearns looks nervous

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (773 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening.
  • It has been revealed that the $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team.
  • Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening. Two-time Cy Young winning left-hander Tarik Skubal has agreed to a record nine-year, $450 million contract with the Latest York Mets. There's a $45 million signing bonus and $30 million in deferred payments. The team has not yet confirmed the signing but that should happen soon.

It has been revealed that the $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team. The $50 million average annual salary also shatters the previous record for a pitcher. That was $43.3 million for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander during their time with the Mets.

Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.

Industry observers note that let's start with the obvious: Skubal's a winner because he signed a massive, record-shattering contract. Sign a record deal and you're always a winner in my book. The Mets are a winner because they landed not just the best free agent on the market, but one of the game's best pitchers. Skubal is a power player who can swing a postseason race or a postseason series all by himself. There are very few players like that in the game and now the Mets have one to lead their rotation.

Industry observers note that boras, Skubal's agent, tends to shatter records, not beat them by just a little bit. Alex Rodriguez's contract with the Rangers is his Mona Lisa: A-Rod's $252 million contract was exactly double the largest contract in the four major North American sports leagues at the time (Kevin Garnett's $126 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves). Boras did it again with Skubal. He obliterated Yamamoto's total guarantee record, Scherzer's and Verlander's shared average annual value record, and also Max Fried's record deal for a lefty ($218 million). Once again, Boras won major.

We can add the Padres here too since they were one of the four teams to meet with Skubal in person this past week, though it was always hard to see San Diego beating out the Blue Jays, Dodgers, and Mets. The Dodgers reportedly held the line at a short-term, high-dollar contract similar to Kyle Tucker's deal, which put them at a disadvantage. Still, they no longer have Skubal in their rotation, and he's irreplaceable. The Blue Jays have been trying to sign top free agents for years (Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Juan Soto, etc.) and have yet to land the plane. Point is, these teams met and pursued Skubal, then he signed elsewhere. Ergo, losers.

According to recent reports, with Skubal off the board, the market for second- and third-tier free agent starters should rapidly pick up. That group includes Michael King, Freddy Peralta, and Trevor Rogers. Skubal signing this early is a massive win for everyone, really, and especially the other free agent starters. They have more than a week to negotiate and sign before the owners are expected to lock out the players after the current CBA expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1. Pitchers are coming off the board fast and furious right now. Expect that to continue for another week or so.

To be sure, the Mets' president of baseball operations is a winner because his team now employs Skubal. This is 100% a Steve Cohen contract, though. Stearns has been against long-term contracts for pitchers throughout his career as an executive, even if he said during the GM Meetings that he works on a "case-by-case basis," and it's hard to believe he'd give a pitcher with three elbow surgeries on his resume this contract. It seems likely Cohen was the one pushing this deal across the finish line, and hey, he's the owner; he can do whatever he wants. Stearns is very much against long-term deals for pitchers, though. I imagine he feels at least a wee bit nervous. Plus, he really can't afford another disaster season like 2026.

Sources indicate that once again, the top free agent went with a major market team. The Mets are signing Skubal this offseason. The Dodgers signed Tucker last offseason. The Mets signed Soto the offseason before that. The Dodgers signed Ohtani the offseason before that. The folks who insist baseball needs a salary cap, both the owners themselves and the fans who lean that way, now have more ammunition for their fight. Settle in. It is very, very likely we're in for months of salary cap debate during an extended lockout. That was true even before Skubal signed.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals.
  • Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North.
  • In a recent development, will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals. Washington enters this game having won two of its last three since returning from the bye. The Commanders scored a come-from-behind victory over the division rival Fresh York Giants last week, keeping their hopes alive in the NFC East in the process. Jayden Daniels and Co. are still just 3-5-1 on the season, but given the relative weaknesses of the NFC East, they can count themselves as divisional contenders if they can string together some wins over the next few weeks.

Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North. The Bengals are red hot, having won five in a row while scoring at least 31 points in each of those contests. Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are tearing holes in opposing defenses, and Cincinnati's own defense is much improved since last year. The Bengals can open up a two-game lead in the division with a win on Monday night.

In a recent development, will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling? We'll find out soon enough as kickoff is approaching. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.

According to recent reports, joe Burrow enters this game as the MVP favorite and the hottest quarterback in the NFL. Burrow is leading the NFL in completions, completion percentage, touchdowns, first downs, yards per game, success rate, passer rating and QBR while ranking second in EPA per play, according to Tru Media.

Over the last five games, he is practically touching the surface of the sun, completing 77.6% of his passes at an average of 8.9 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdown passes and three interceptions. He's totaled at least four scores in each of those five games, tying a league-record streak. During that stretch, his 0.42 EPA per dropback mark is more than 50% better than the second-place player, Trevor Lawrence (0.26), per Tru Media. He is shredding every single coverage with ease.

In a recent development, ja'Marr Chase is on nearly as much of a heater as is Burrow. Chase has a 43-666-4 receiving line since the Bengals' Week 5, and he's recorded at least 10 catches for 141 yards in each of the Bengals' last three games. Last week, he went off for 231 yards against the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers — the fourth 200-plus-yard game of his career. The Commanders, needless to say, do not have anybody who has a hope of guarding him.

The Commies have been known to double opposing No. 1 wideouts more often than other teams this season, but even doing that might not necessarily be wise because Tee Higgins is playing the best football of his career as well. Higgins has a 53-824-6 receiving line so far this season, as he's averaging a career-best 91.6 receiving yards per game. He's been a bit quieter than Chase over the last two weeks, but he still has 10 grabs for 88 yards and two touchdowns in that time. His size and physicality make him a nightmare matchup for any cornerback, especially with Burrow playing as well as he is at the moment.

Meanwhile, the Commanders have allowed the NFL's fourth-most completions to tight ends so far this season, as well as the second-most yards and touchdowns. That could open up opportunities for Mike Gesicki and/or Drew Sample, though Gesicki is obviously the bigger receiving threat of the two.

According to recent reports, washington has actually been somewhat solid against the run this season, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. Opposing offensive lines have cleared the way for only 1.08 yards before contact per rush, according to Tru Media, and the second-level defenders have limited rushers to the third-lowest broken tackle rate in the league.

However, the Bengals basically only run the ball as an occasional changeup, with Chase Brown and Samaje Perine acting as receivers nearly as often as they do runners. Even if the Commanders shut down the run game, it seems unlikely to matter much to Cincinnati's offensive success. Everything runs through Burrow, Chase and Higgins.

It has been revealed that jayden Daniels has been efficient since his return from his elbow injury, completing 67.3% of his passes at an average of 7.6 yards per attempt. He has seven touchdowns and two interceptions, along with 180 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries across five games during which the Commanders have compiled a 2-2-1 record. Daniels hasn't been particularly explosive during that stretch, but he has kept the chains moving for the most part, and the Commies have been able to stay in games against the Giants (twice) and Eagles while losing by only one score to the 49ers and Rams.

Without Terry McLaurin, Daniels' top targets are Stefon Diggs, rookie Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Van Jefferson and tight end Chig Okonkwo.

Diggs is mostly a short-area target who splits his time between the perimeter and the slot. He works the underneath zones as Daniels tries to matriculate the ball down the field. Williams has become a bigger part of the rotation in recent weeks but hasn't really popped off that much despite the increase in role. Burks is a rotational deep threat who has seen his snap share increase since McLaurin went down, while Jefferson works in behind each of the top three. Okonkwo is a short-area chain mover similar to Diggs, but with perhaps more run-after-catch ability relative to his position.

It has been revealed that the Bengals are surprisingly 12th in the NFL in net yards allowed per attempt (which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks), and they have allowed only 11 passing touchdowns so far this season. They have a solid enough group of defensive backs, including one star in DJ Turner II, and their tackling has improved significantly on the second level of the defense this year.

The Commanders don't have much of a run game to speak of, what with their stable of backs combining to average just 3.7 yards per carry this season. They'll get Jacory Croskey-Merritt back on Monday night, but even he is only at 3.6 yards per carry this season. He's likely to split work with both Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler, each of whom is better in the passing game than they are when running the football.

According to recent reports, with big Dexter Lawrence in the middle of the defensive line, it could be difficult for Washington to get anything going on the ground, even though the Bengals have actually been hit for 5.0 yards per opponent rush attempt so far this season. Lawrence has near single-handedly taken over a few games or stretches of possessions, even if teams like the Dolphins, Titans and Falcons have been able to find holes on the ground.

The current version of the Commanders does not have the firepower to keep up with the Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins show. I'm not sure any version of the Commanders ever did, but even in winning two of their last three games, they haven't exactly looked impressive. The Bengals, meanwhile, are putting on an aerial assault for the ages every week. Pick: Bengals 31, Commanders 20.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Harden is in the midst of his worst scoring season since his second year in Oklahoma City 16 years ago, but the 37-year-old turned back the clock some on Friday night with a 51-point performance in a Cavaliers win over the Pacers.

Harden's vintage scoring night saw him go 15-of-26 from the field and 14-of-14 from the free-throw line in typical Harden fashion for the 26th 50-point game of his career. That moves him into third all-time in NBA history for 50-point games, passing Kobe Bryant and sitting just five behind Michael Jordan.

At 37 years old (and 86 days), Harden is the fourth-oldest player to score 50 points in an NBA game, passing LeBron James on that list and trailing only Bryant, Jordan and Jamal Crawford, who scored 50 at 39 years old.

After the game, Cavaliers' coach Kenny Atkinson offered an eyebrow-raising comment calling Harden "top-10 all-time," which drew immediate pushback from NBA fans, but Harden is an unquestioned Hall of Famer and continues to put his name among the all-time greats on NBA scoring lists.

His co-star in Cleveland, Donovan Mitchell, lamented that Harden doesn't get the appreciation he deserves at this stage of his career, and that he expects, much like Russell Westbrook, that it won't happen until he retires.

Industry observers note that "He won't until it's over with," Mitchell stated. "I hate it, but that's just the world we live in. We won't appreciate greatness. We didn't appreciate Russ in his latter years until now. It's like, 'Oh man, Russ was this and that.' It's like we forgot he averaged 28, 15 and 16 for a month. It's one of those things where we live in such a negative space. I hate it. At the end of the day, he doesn't care. And for me, seeing that, I don't care. It helps, but at the end of the day, that's just what the world is. It sucks that that's that way, but us in this locker room and guys in this league, we know who he is and we know what he's done for the game. That goes for not just him but a lot of people in this league. We don't appreciate what's in front of us on a consistent basis.".

Harden has long been a divisive player among NBA fans. Some have appreciated his ruthless efficiency while others have hated the aesthetics of his mastery of the dark arts of drawing fouls. As Mitchell noted, few players have had as much influence over the game in the last decade-plus as Harden. From his massive stepback 3-pointer to his movement on drives to create contact, so much of Harden's game has made its way into the arsenal of most elite guard scorers.

It has been revealed that fans will debate whether that's a good thing, but his influence is undeniable. As Mitchell mentioned, whenever Harden calls it a career, he will get more appreciation, but there will also be heated debates over his place in NBA history as one of the most divisive stars (from a play-style perspective, at least) of his generation.

Te voorzichtig of een gevolg van het WK-format? Nederland-Japan 2:2

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Nederland speelde tegen Japan in balbezit vanuit een duidelijke 1-4-3-3-basisformatie, met zeer lage backs, duidelijke spelers die voor de breedte zorgden, een echte spits (Malen) en twee nummers tien (Rijnders en Gravenberch).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 19.06.2026 in den Kategorien National Teams,Uncategorized mit 1 Kommentar.

According to recent reports, de twee favorieten van de groep stonden tegenover elkaar. “Dat regelen we wel in de andere wedstrijden” had zomaar het motto van beide ploegen kunnen zijn.

Nederland speelde tegen Japan in balbezit vanuit een duidelijke 1-4-3-3-basisformatie, met zeer lage backs, duidelijke spelers die voor de breedte zorgden, een echte spits (Malen) en twee nummers tien (Rijnders en Gravenberch).

Japan verdedigde vanuit een 1-5-4-1-middenblok, stuurde het spel naar buiten en zette alleen bij Nederlandse doeltrappen hoger druk. Om vanuit het middenblok over te schakelen naar een actiever, meer sturend middenblok met druk op de flank, schoof Maeda aan de linkerkant (op papier de linker tien in het 1-5-4-1) door naar de eerste pressinglijn en zette hij samen met wingback Nakamura druk op Dumfries. Daardoor werd De Jong vaak als vrije nummer zes losjes afgeschermd door de Japanse dubbele zes en de zeer terugverdedigende spits Ueda. Japan zette zijn pressing alleen heel situationeel in, goed afgestemd tussen de voorste en middelste lijn, wanneer een breedtepass gevolgd werd door een korte terugpass. Daardoor waren zowel de actie als de vervolgactie goed te voorspellen en waren de passlijnen kort en makkelijk te belopen.

Nederlandse controlfreaks met één uitzondering.

Voor Nederland lag in balbezit, binnen het zeer positievaste en vooral statische 1-4-3-3, een sterke focus op controle in de wedstrijd. Daarbij werden ook de technisch sterke centrale verdedigers met korte passafstanden nadrukkelijk betrokken als opbouwers. In veel oefenwedstrijden en Nations League-duels vormde Van de Ven als linksback vaak een soort driemansopbouw doordat hij laag bleef, terwijl Dumfries hoger doorschoof. Tegen diepere of passievere blokken ontstond zo vaak een soort 1-3-2-4-1. In deze wedstrijd bleef echter ook Dumfries in het begin vrijwel uitsluitend onderdeel van de opbouwlijn. Naarmate de wedstrijd vorderde werd Dumfries, in tegenstelling tot Nederland als geheel, wel moediger en schoof hij af en toe door naar de halfspace of zelfs zonder bal mee de zestien in.

Voor De Jong, die zoals altijd heel dicht bij de opbouwlijn zijn positie koos, maakten beide achten die tussen de Japanse linies speelden zoveel mogelijk ruimte vrij. De Nederlandse opbouwlijn probeerde de afstand voor de Japanse voorste lijn te vergroten door met een vlakke viermansopbouw te spelen. Daarbij lieten ze af en toe zien welke kwaliteit er door het centrum mogelijk is, vooral via Van Dijk en De Jong (soms samen met een tijdelijk terugzakkende Rijnders), wanneer ze druk kunnen uitlokken door de grote afstanden van de backs en vervolgens centraal door kunnen spelen.

Japan was zich daar echter van bewust en liet zich maar zelden verleiden. Daardoor speelde Nederland steeds opnieuw in een grote “U” rond het Japanse blok. Nederland nam geen risicovolle beslissingen en gebruikte balbezit vooral als verdedigend middel om geen fouten te maken of Japanse counters weg te geven. Een veelgebruikte toernooitactiek voor technisch en individueel sterkere teams.

Door het overtal in de opbouw en de focus op simpele passes werden gevaarlijke balverliezen in het centrum vermeden, ondersteund door een degelijke restverdediging. Maar zo extreem als hier — met een vlakke viermansopbouw, extreem positievaste tienen (geen overbelasting, niet actief om de bal vragen) en vrijwel geen dribbels behalve van de brede buitenspelers in hogere posities — bleef vooral de vraag hoe Nederland zelf kansen wilde creëren.

Recent findings suggest that een terugkerend, bijna consequent patroon in de Nederlandse opbouw was het bewust opschuiven via de linkerkant. Vooral Gakpo werd vaak in één-tegen-één-situaties gebracht dankzij goede bindende loopacties van Rijnders. Gakpo koos echter niet voor een directe actie tegen zijn tegenstander, maar juist voor een licht vertragende dribbel met als doel een vrije passhoek naar binnen te creëren. Dat had ook een nadeel: extra Japanse spelers konden achter de bal komen en ruimtes afsluiten in zijn één-tegen-één.

Sources indicate that de reden daarvoor lag in het Nederlandse idee om Donyell Malen, die zich tijdens de opbouw nauwelijks met het spel bemoeide, in de voeten aan te spelen. Daar kon hij met zijn wendbaarheid goed standhouden en was hij vervelend om te verdedigen.

Industry observers note that aan de andere kant werd er via de rechterkant langzaam opgebouwd. Dat gebeurde door een klassieke positiewisseling tussen Summerville en Dumfries of via lange diagonale verplaatsingen van Van Dijk naar Summerville, steeds met oog voor een goede verdedigende positie.

Recent findings suggest that malen had ook vaker al eerder tijdens de opbouw gezocht of aangespeeld kunnen worden. Maar of hij die momenten zelf niet herkende, of dat de Nederlandse aanpak van defensief balbezit dit simpelweg niet toeliet, blijft de vraag.

Daarom begon Gravenberch al vrij vroeg als balverre nummer tien de centrale ruimtes achter de Japanse dubbele zes te bezetten. Zijn ploeggenoten deden echter weinig met die bewegingen — bijvoorbeeld door kort naar binnen te dribbelen of doordat Rijnders uitweek — waardoor Gravenberch daar uiteindelijk weer mee stopte.

Eenvoud als middel om fouten te vermijden had zomaar het oranje motto van deze wedstrijd kunnen zijn.

In a recent development, toch ontstond de beste Nederlandse aanval juist door meer risico te nemen. Een pass tussen de linies naar Gravenberch, een dribbel in een 1-tegen-2, een overlap van Dumfries waardoor de 1-tegen-1 van Summerville veranderde in een 2-tegen-1 en uiteindelijk een vrije schietkans ontstond. Allemaal elementen die veel te weinig terugkwamen in deze wedstrijd.

Wanneer Japan nog verder terugzakte in een extreem compact 5-4-1-blok rond het eigen strafschopgebied, positioneerden de Nederlandse backs zich iets meer diagonaal tussen centrale verdediger en buitenspeler en kwamen ze dus iets meer naar binnen.

Een laag blok is geen doel op zich.

Verdedigend koos Nederland bij Japanse doeltrappen voor een zeer mangeoriënteerde aanpak. Ze stuurden de Japanse opbouw naar de zwakkere voet van de speler aan de bal om zo een zo onnauwkeurig mogelijke lange bal en een luchtduel uit te lokken. In de lucht hadden de Nederlanders immers een duidelijk voordeel.

Voor de rest liet Nederland zich meestal terugzakken in een vrij passieve 1-5-4-1, waarbij De Jong vaak de laatste lijn aanvulde om Doan, Kubo of de rechter tien van Japan te volgen.

Sources indicate that nederland was heel duidelijk gefocust op het afdekken van de diepte en wilde absoluut geen ruimte achter of voor de verdediging weggeven. Daardoor kwam de Nederlandse dubbele zes in een lastig dilemma terecht tussen hun mandekking en de verticale compactheid ten opzichte van de laatste lijn van Oranje, die in twijfelgevallen eerder achteruit dan vooruit verdedigde.

Een enkele spits in een 1-5-4-1 heeft het meestal moeilijk, maar Malen probeerde ook niet echt functies op zich te nemen die zijn ploeg konden helpen. Tegelijk waren de buitenste spelers van het blok vooral bezig met hun verticale mandekking op de Japanse driemansopbouw. Daardoor zette Nederland vrijwel geen druk op de Japanse opbouw, die zich vrij kon ontwikkelen.

Het zeer beweeglijke en rotatierijke aanvalsspel van Japan tegenover de fysieke, grote Nederlandse spelers liet vooral potentieel zien wanneer Japan vroeg naar de flank speelde en vervolgens naar binnen combineerde.

Door het gebrek aan druk van Nederland kon Japan vanuit de opbouwlijn schone en snelle passcombinaties uitvoeren naar een hoog gepositioneerde wingback. Vanaf daar kon die relatief eenvoudig naar binnen spelen, omdat de pressingafstanden van de Nederlandse backs te groot waren om al bij de eerste aanname druk te zetten.

Kort gezegd kon Japan, door de — in deze context — veel te late druk van Nederland, sneller en zuiverder naar de flank spelen dan Nederland in staat was om daar druk op te krijgen. Want als de Nederlandse backs eerder zouden uitstappen, zouden ze veel verder naar buiten worden getrokken, wat weer haaks stond op het Nederlandse idee om het centrum en de diepte gesloten te houden.

It has been revealed that vanaf de flank kon Japan vervolgens profiteren van het eerder beschreven dilemma van de Nederlandse dubbele zes. Die moest nu kiezen tussen het blijven volgen van hun directe tegenstander (zoals Rijnders vaak deed), waardoor ruimte vóór de verdediging ontstond, of terugzakken richting de laatste lijn, waardoor er voor hen geen druk meer op de bal was.

Door verloren één-tegen-één-duels in het centrum, problemen in het volgen van tegenstanders en de algemene passiviteit van het blok kwam Japan uiteindelijk ook op gelijke hoogte. Na een gebrek aan duidelijke afspraken bij het winnen van terrein konden de Japanners het strafschopgebied binnendringen en werden ze tot aan het schot eigenlijk alleen maar begeleid.

Ironisch genoeg werd juist Dumfries’ actieve manier van verdedigen hem fataal, omdat hij zijn benen opende en daarmee de korte hoek vrijgaf voor Nakamura.

Sources indicate that daar kwam nog bij dat naast De Jong ook Van Hecke en vooral Van Dijk moeite hadden met korte, diepe loopacties. Mede door het gebrek aan afdekking hadden ze problemen om die goed te volgen.

According to recent reports, door gebrekkige timing en onvoldoende precisie wist Japan daar uiteindelijk niet optimaal van te profiteren. Omdat De Jong geen natuurlijke centrale verdediger is, werd de diepte soms niet goed bewaakt door de laatste lijn. Daarnaast kozen Van Dijk en Van Hecke geregeld een andere hoogte dan De Jong, iets wat Japan eigenlijk te weinig uitbuitte.

Een kleine aanpassing die weinig opleverde.

In de loop van de wedstrijd paste Nederland de aanloophoeken aan. Daardoor veranderde automatisch ook de positie van de buitenste spelers van de middenlinie. Zij konden nu iets losser uit de lijn stappen richting de hoog opgeschoven Japanse wingbacks en druk zetten op indribbelende of terugzakkende Japanse opbouwers. Zo kon Japan minder makkelijk direct naar de flank spelen zoals eerder beschreven.

Toch klopten zowel het moment als de richting van die acties niet. Daardoor stonden spelers als Gakpo en Koopmeiners hoger op het veld, maar konden ze na een succesvolle Japanse pass niet meer meeverdedigen in dezelfde actie.

In plaats daarvan hingen ze vaak een beetje tussen wal en schip. Opmerkelijk genoeg sloten ze niet de terugpass af — wat de één-tegen-één-verdediging op de flank juist geholpen zou hebben — maar probeerden ze alsnog aansluiting te houden bij de actie. Daardoor kregen de Japanse wingbacks juist meer ruimte aan de zijkant en werd ook het verleggen van het spel makkelijker.

Sources indicate that grotere defensieve problemen ontstonden ook wanneer de Nederlandse flankduo’s rotaties moesten verdedigen, vooral aan de kant van Gakpo. Waar Koopmeiners kwaliteiten heeft in het volgen van zijn directe tegenstander, verloor Gakpo af en toe zijn man uit het oog.

Opvallend kwetsbaar was Nederland bovendien in de organisatie van de verdediging bij corners en ingooien.

Bij de weinige balveroveringen waren zowel de besluitvorming als de omschakelkracht van Nederland te zwak om echt gevaarlijk te worden.

In a recent development, daarnaast werd de horizontale compactheid in de slotfase steeds slechter, waardoor Japan steeds vaker vrije spelers tussen de linies vond. De vraag is of dat vooral een fysiek probleem was of eerder een cognitief en organisatorisch probleem.

De verdedigende strategie versterkte en veroorzaakte individuele probleme.

According to recent reports, ook De Jongs manier van dekken past niet echt bij de zeer directe en doorjagende stijl van Van Dijk en Van Hecke. Waar die twee hun tegenstander vanuit de laatste lijn vaak strak blijven volgen, houdt De Jong zich als balverre speler vaker bezig met het (her)organiseren van de verdediging. Daardoor ontstaan er vrije spelers tussen de linies, zeker omdat de Nederlandse dubbele zes ook nog eens mangeoriënteerd verdedigt.

Wanneer De Jong wél uitstapt uit de laatste lijn, laat hij soms problemen zien in het daadwerkelijk druk zetten, vooral qua dynamiek nadat hij de eerste aanname van zijn tegenstander heeft verdedigd. Japan maakte daar richting het einde van de wedstrijd meerdere keren gebruik van om de balcirculatie in hogere zones netjes voort te zetten en het spel te verleggen.

Later in de wedstrijd werd De Jong vervangen door Aké.

It has been revealed that ook aan de andere kant viel op dat vooral Van Dijk moeite had met het oppakken en volgen van de snelle wisselbewegingen van de Japanners, met name bij korte bewegingen in de diepte (zie afbeelding). Door zijn directe, mangeoriënteerde manier van verdedigen kwam hij daarbij af en toe in de problemen. Japan wist daar echter niet van te profiteren door een gebrek aan timing en precisie. Over het geheel genomen waren er dus meerdere individual-tactische tekortkomingen zichtbaar die niet goed aansloten bij de gekozen passieve verdedigende strategie.

In balbezit beschikt Nederland over veel individuele kwaliteit. Als een tegenstander in de val loopt, kan Nederland via alle spelers in het centrum dynamiek creëren. De aanpak van defensief balbezit was echter behoorlijk extreem en zorgde voor weinig doelkansen, maar wel voor veel controle over de wedstrijd.

Waarschijnlijk was het plan om Malen vaker vrij te spelen vanaf de flank en hem zo beter in het spel te betrekken. Desondanks heeft Nederland, zelfs met kleine aanpassingen waarbij iets meer risico wordt genomen, enorm veel potentie om gevaarlijk aanvallend voetbal te spelen en tegen iedere tegenstander tot kansen en doelpunten te komen.

It has been revealed that wat vanuit Nederlands perspectief eerder zorgen zou moeten baren, is de defensieve organisatie. De balans tussen druk zetten en het afsluiten van het centrum en de tussenruimtes klopt niet. De druk ligt op zo’n laag prioriteitsniveau dat voor iedere degelijke ploeg op dit toernooi het vinden van de juiste veldbezetting en het opschuiven geen echte uitdaging vormt. De sluitende bewegingen van de Nederlandse spelers zorgen daardoor eerder voor schadebeperking dan voor het daadwerkelijk voorkomen van gevaar. Hun bewegingen worden als het ware zonder enige vorm van druk volledig geneutraliseerd.

Ook de laatste lijn en de verdediging van het eigen strafschopgebied ogen niet extreem goed op elkaar afgestemd. Problemen in de mandekkingen op de flank, vrijwel geen mogelijkheden om te counteren vanwege de lage en op mandekking gebaseerde posities, en een algemene slaperigheid bij standaardsituaties kunnen Nederland al in de groepsfase flink parten spelen.

In Nederland zorgde de invalbeurt van Depay bij een stand van 2-1 voor veel verbazing onder de toeschouwers. In werkelijkheid wist hij niet echt acties toe te voegen die Oranje verder hielpen.

Wel moet worden gezegd dat de positie van enige spits voor een diep, naar achteren gericht en passief 1-5-4-1-blok tegen een tegenstander die opbouwt in een 3-2-structuur weinig invloedrijke mogelijkheden biedt.

Toch zou een dynamischere spits, die meer loopt en diepgang brengt, Nederland vooral bij balveroveringen en omschakelmomenten waarschijnlijk meer hebben geholpen dan Depay in deze wedstrijd deed.

HH groeide op aan de Nederlands-Duitse grens, maar keek op tactisch vlak liever richting Zuid-Europa. Naast zijn werkzaamheden als freelancer voor Duitse profclubs is hij sinds twee jaar ook actief als jeugdtrainer bij de O17 van N.E.C. Nijmegen.

It has been revealed that LL ontdekte zijn fascinatie voor voetbalinhoud en tactiek dankzij de vernieuwende ideeën van Tuchel bij Mainz. In de regio rond de Narrenstadt is hij al actief geweest binnen zowel het amateurvoetbal als de jeugdopleidingen van profclubs (NLZ).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Newly introduced York Mets' splash record signing of ace lefty Tarik Skubal, who was far and away the top free agent available, has of course reset the market in a major way. Those who missed out on Skubal and those aspiring contenders who otherwise have rotation needs may be left wondering: What's next?

According to recent reports, clubs like the Chicago Cubs, Atlanta Braves, San Diego Padres, Los Angeles Dodgers, Chicago White Sox, Tampa Bay Rays, among others, still have options, even if none of them rise to the skyscraping level of Mr. Skubal. Let's explore some possibilities for you, and let's also move beyond just the current class of free agents and name-check some potential trade targets who could buttress a rotation for next season and beyond. Let's jump in.

In a recent development, yes, Morejon is a reliever at this writing, but his deep repertoire, excellent velocity and stuff make him a compelling transition candidate for next season, even with recent reporting that he wants to stay in the bullpen. Morejon, who sits triple digits, can give some velocity back while working longer outings and still have plenty in the tank to miss bats in the strike zone. And if starting doesn't work, he can go right back to dominating as a reliever. He doesn't turn 28 until February.

While his ERA ballooned last season thanks to some early season struggles, Rogers' underlying performance indicators are still quite strong, specifically his ability to get chase out of the zone and duck quality contact with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years. He's not a name that leaps readily to mind, but Rogers has a high ceiling and bargain potential.

Recent findings suggest that peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the New York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter, all the way to ALCS MVP. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form. The 2027 season will be his age-31 campaign.

Recent findings suggest that he has a full, five-pitch repertoire with elite spin and movement on almost all of those five offerings and boasts an ERA+ of 129 for his career. King turns 32 in May, and he's experienced a gradual decline at the command-and-control level over the past few seasons. As well, his fastball's not beating hitters in the zone like it used to. That's to say, there's risk here, but even if he's beginning his decline phase, King will be a rotation asset for the near- to mid-term.

Industry observers note that the 32-year-old righty was reborn last season after a deadline trade to the Braves. Atlanta ramped up his splitter usage and adjusted his slider shape, and in perhaps related matters, Mahle was much more successful at staying away from the heart of the zone. In 54 ⅓ innings after the trade, Mahle ran a sub-2.00 ERA and struck out 48 batters against nine walks. No, he's not going to put up those numbers over the long haul, but his revival makes him an intriguing option.

Industry observers note that the big pre-Skubal hot stove news was the San Francisco Giants' reported willingness to listen to offers on ace Logan Webb. Among sports fans, Carmelo Anthony is perhaps most synonymous with Upcoming York -- both upstate from his incredible year at Syracuse and in New York City, where he starred for the Knicks. But Anthony was raised in Baltimore and is extremely proud of his roots.

Recent findings suggest that anthony joined that group on Friday with an Instagram post that called on Humphrey to go beyond the apology he issued earlier in the week. Anthony wants Humphrey to join him, Scott, and others in the community to find ways to lead by example.

Industry observers note that I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's in my blood. I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take fro you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. And it doesn't get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment.

Marlon, I see the apology. I'll take it, man to man. But Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does. I put my time, energy and resources in Baltimore because I want kids to have somebody who believe in them. That's the job when you wear this city on your chest. You don't get to rep Baltimore on Sundays and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday.

So let me tell you what Baltimore makes. We make fighters. We make builders. We make people who were counted out from the day they were born and showed up anyway. We make teachers who buy supplies out of their own pockets, coaches who become fathers, artists the whole world copies, and returning citizens who turn their pain into purpose. It has been revealed that baltimore doesn't make criminals. Baltimore makes the ones who make it out. And the ones who come back. #B-MORE.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the NFL will not suspend DK Metcalf for his actions during the Pittsburgh Steelers' recent loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, according to a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter. Metcalf was ejected late in the third quarter after committing his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

During his Monday media availability, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy remarked that he and Metcalf spoke about the situation, calling the conversations "productive." He added that any additional discipline ffrom the Steelers would be kept internal.

"Life's about learning situations," McCarthy stated. "I do believe in second chances. I will judge him based on my personal interaction with him. I did appreciate the way he communicated today.".

Sunday's ejection marks Metcalf's third ejection in his eight-season career. Metcalf was also suspended for the final two games of the 2025 regular season after getting into a physical confrontation with a Lions fan. He returned for the playoffs but dropped a key pass early in Pittsburgh's eventual 30-6 loss to Houston.

Metcalf was already fined earlier this year for an unsportsmanlike penalty during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns. It was the latest in a series of fines Metcalf has accrued during his NFL career.

Sources indicate that metcalf's fines have totaled a whopping $245,647, according to Spotrac. This does not include an additional $555,555 fine attached to his two-game suspension for the Lions fan altercation.

In a recent development, while his actions have hurt his wallet, his lack of production has hurt the Steelers on the field. Outside of his 11-catch performance against the Buccaneers in Week 6, Metcalf has had over five receptions in a game just once this season. He's had just six catches in Pittsburgh's last four games. He had one catch for just two yards before being ejected from Sunday's game after trying to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye.

Metcalf, 28, hasn't been the same player since he signed a four-year, $132 million contract with Pittsburgh shortly after he was traded from Seattle. Last year (his first in Pittsburgh), Metcalf caught 59 passes for 850 yards, which were both career lows. His six touchdown catches tied a career low.

Recent findings suggest that his lack of production and on-field problems have led to questions about his future with the Steelers. For now, all that is known is that Metcalf will be available for Friday's big showdown between Pittsburgh and Denver.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books. So it's really saying something to start registering all-time marks of franchise ineptitude, which is precisely what the Warriors have done over the last week.

After battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history. The only other time this has happened to a Warriors team was in February of 1998, a few months after Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo. The total margin of that four-game losing streak was 104 points.

This current one is even worse. These Warriors have lost their last four by 109 points, and what makes it even more jarring is comparing them to the team that had won eight straight prior to Curry's injury. That 1997-98 team was trash all year, starting 1-14 and finishing with just 19 wins without ever winning more than three straight games.

These Warriors, on the other hand, were starting to look like a legitimate playoff-caliber team. A cynic would say that run of victories came against a softer schedule than what they have faced of late, but that qualification doesn't hold much, if any, water. That eight-game run included wins over the Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat and an Orlando Magic team that has immediately gone on to win five of its last six.

Perhaps the Warriors would have lost to the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs even with Curry. Hell, maybe they would've lost to the Latest Orleans Pelicans, Dallas Mavericks and Memphis Grizzlies, too. That feels unlikely, but who knows? Even with Curry, the Warriors aren't good enough to start checking off scheduled wins. But that's not the point.

The point is how utterly incapable they have looked in losing these games. Not only have they lost each of these last four by at least 20 points, but they've also been held under 100 points in all of them. That's a combination of incompetence that stretches beyond a franchise mark. That hasn't happened to a single other team this century.

In a recent development, before we try to answer that, let's just agree upfront that Curry has little to no chance of actually winning what would be his third MVP. The Warriors almost certainly won't have a good enough record to put him in real contention. His across-the-board counting stats, even if he were to maintain his torrid early pace, are not going to match those of Luka Dončić or Victor Wembanyama.

According to recent reports, the only real chance would be if both of those guys, and likely a bunch of others, failed to meet the 65-game threshold, but the chances of Curry, who has already missed six games and isn't expected to be re-evaluated until around Thanksgiving, making it to 65 games himself already feel next to impossible. He may be past the maximum 17 games-missed mark before he even returns from this injury.

According to recent reports, which is to say, what we're asking here is whether Curry, at 38 years old and in his 18th season, is still the most valuable player in the league (has he always been?), not whether he'll actually win the award, and the answer to that question, at least in its simplest form, could very well lie in his absence. Just look at this team without him.

Eight-game win streak with Curry.

Four-game losing streak without Curry.

According to recent reports, admittedly, there's some cherry-picking in those numbers. Curry actually didn't play in one of the wins during that eight-game streak, and the Warriors still beat the Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with a 122.8 offensive rating behind 37 points from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

It has been revealed that we're also leaving out the aforementioned game against the Rockets on Nov. 11 in which Curry only played six minutes and the Warriors looked fine, or even good, in testing one of the best teams in the league to its limit. It also must be noted that Golden State lost its first three games of the season and looked every bit like the team many of us predicted would stink, all of which Curry played in.

Sources indicate that still, the general rule applies. The Warriors go as Curry goes. That was true even in the golden years when the on/off splits, even with the likes of Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson still out there, always pointed to Curry as the clear MVP.

"If I didn't have Steph, I would've been like every other NBA coach and lasted a few years [with the Warriors] and then gone and coached somewhere else," Steve Kerr has said, openly admitting that Curry, and Curry alone, has been the difference between a journeyman coaching career and a Hall-of-Fame one.

He's not lying. Have a look at the numbers.

Even if you want to remove the 2019-20 season from the equation, when Durant had defected, Thompson missed the whole year and Curry only played in five games, Kerr is still a below-.500 coach at 74-96 without Curry in the lineup. This is a coach who has had all kinds of great players at his disposal over the years, and still it was always Curry in control of his and the organization's ultimate fate.

This is still the case for the Warriors, who continue to fall off a cliff without Curry. When he's been on the floor this year, they have registered a 59.6 eFG%, which would rank first in the league. When he's off, they fall to 49.1%, which would rank last.

Even the defensive decline we see in Curry's on/off splits can largely be tied back to his offense. Without him, the Warriors are unable to create the same shots and, when their newly introduced brand of shots miss far more often, they end up defending in transition on almost 3% more possessions. That's a massive deal. It's meant almost five more points per game surrendered to fast breaks over this stretch.

Sources indicate that the Warriors have produced an average offensive rating of 103.8 in games Curry hasn't played this year, which would rank as the second-worst mark in the league. All told, they are 26.3 points per 100 possessions better in Curry's minutes this season, per Cleaning The Glass. By comparison, the Lakers drop by 25.5 points per 100 when Dončić sits. Wembanyama is in his own galaxy with this stat, representing a 37.8-point decline in San Antonio when he's off the floor.

It's fair to say Wembanyama means as much to San Antonio's defense, where most of that decline happens, as Curry does to Golden State's offense, and certainly the Lakers falling off by as much as they do offensively, even with Austin Reaves as a legit secondary star, tells you everything you need to know about his impact. All of these guys are MVP players.

But only one, by subjective definition, can be the most valuable, and the simple truth is the Lakers and Spurs are outfitted with far more functional rosters independent of their respective superstars. In Golden State, there is just nowhere else to turn. Nobody to generate any kind of consistent offensive leverage. No gravity. No shot creation.

After the Warriors took that 38-point beating against the Spurs without Curry, the rookie Lendeborg, who had, in total unfairness, been saddled with filling Curry's go-to-scorer shoes, said "it felt helpless out there," and that is exactly what it has looked like since the Curry variable was removed from Golden State's equation.

To be fair, the absence of a player is an imperfect lens through which to view value for a bunch of contextual reasons, not the least of which is how a team like Golden State is designed to play -- a specific, Curry-centric ecosystem not particularly amenable to abrupt adjustments. These players are not as bad as they have looked without Curry over these last four games.

Recent findings suggest that but by the same token, they aren't close to as good as they looked with Curry, either. I always laugh when my dad calls me saying things like, "This Pat Spencer guy can play!" Everyone looks like they can play next to Curry. And then he goes away and suddenly you're wondering how the hell this guy made the Washington Generals look like one of the best teams in the league. Is he some kind of miracle worker?

Sources indicate that in a basketball sense, that's not far off. Curry's individual production is already virtually unmatched, but it's his exponential powers, his ability to compound the returns of those around him, that set him apart. It's early, yes. Perhaps the Warriors will figure things out the longer Curry is away. Probably not. But maybe they at least can return to competitive functionality. Until then, however, it's pretty hard to not think Curry is the most valuable player in the league when you watch the Warriors play without him.
